Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verses 1–2:

The Tafsir of Surat Al 'Imran

It is a Medinan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The Shaykh, the Imam, the Most Exalted (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Reports have been transmitted concerning the virtue of this surah and Surat al-Baqarah, among them what is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Learn al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, for they are the two radiant ones (al-zahrawan); they will shade their companion on the Day of Resurrection."

And it is related from him that he said: "al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran will come on the Day of Resurrection as if they were two clouds, or two shades, or two flocks of birds in ranks (furqan min tayr sawaff)."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah﴾

As for the alif, it is (a reference to) Allah; the lam is Jibril (Gabriel); and the mim is Muhammad. And in it there is an indication of what Allah sent down, through the tongue of Jibril, to Muhammad.

We have already mentioned the opinions concerning the letters of the alphabet (huruf al-tahajji).

The mim is given a fatha when joined, even though a sakin letter, when moved, is moved with a kasra; this is because they found a kasra after the jazm (the sukun), and the ya' in it carries a jazm.

﴿There is no god but He﴾: there is no worshipped one besides Him. ﴿The Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence﴾: al-Hayy is the Everlasting who never ceases.

As for al-Qayyum, its explanation has already preceded. It has been said: it is the One who does not cease and does not change. Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr said: He is the One whose existence is permanent. Umar and Ibn Mas'ud recited ﴿al-Hayy al-Qiyam﴾, and this is among the shadha (irregular readings).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verses 3–4:

The words of the Most High: ﴿He has sent down to you the Book with truth﴾. "Al-Kitab" (the Book) is the Qur'an, and it is called a "kitab" because it gathers together the verses and the letters. The root is k-t-b, which means gathering. From it comes "al-katība" (a military unit), which is a detachment, because its members are gathered together.

From the same root one says "kutibat al-baghla" (the she-mule was gathered), when one joins her two vulvar lips with a ring. The words ﴿with truth﴾ mean with truthfulness in its indications, its reports, and its promise and threat.

The words ﴿confirming what is before it﴾ mean: the Qur'an confirms what came before it of the Torah and the Gospel.

He said ﴿what is before it﴾ because it confirms what preceded it and manifests its truthfulness, like a thing present before one's eyes.

﴿And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel before this as guidance for the people﴾. Here He says "anzala" (sent down), while at the beginning He said "nazzala" (sent down gradually) regarding ﴿He sent down the Book﴾, because He sent down the Torah all at once and the Gospel all at once, whereas He sent down the Qur'an in separate parts.

As for the Torah, its origin is "wawriyya", from "al-warā", from their saying "warā al-zand" when it gives light and its fire comes out; and it is said "warā zandī ʿinda fulān" when his affair becomes clear to him. So it was named "wawriyya" for its radiance and for being a light, and the waw was changed into a tā', so it became "tawriyya". As for the Gospel, it is from "al-najl", which is the origin, and it was named thus because it was a foundation among the foundations of knowledge.

﴿And He sent down the Criterion﴾. It is said: it is the Qur'an, which distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful. It is also said: everything Allah sent down is a criterion, because it distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful. In the verse there is an inversion of order, and its meaning is: "And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel before this, and He sent down the Criterion as guidance for the people."

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment﴾. It was revealed concerning the delegation of Najran from the Christians. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and among them were al-Sayyid and al-ʿAqib, two men of theirs. They were sixty riders, and it is said nearly twenty riders. They entered the mosque, and the Prophet (ﷺ) had already prayed the ʿAsr prayer, so they stood and prayed their prayer facing east. When they finished, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked them about ʿIsa, and they differed about him. Some of them said: "He is Allah." Some said: "He is the son of Allah." And some said: "He is the third of three." He said: "Submit." They said: "We are Muslims." He said: "You have lied; what prevents you from that is your saying that ʿIsa is the son of Allah." So Allah sent down concerning them about eighty-some verses, from the beginning of the Surah of Al ʿImran concerning the disputation and the proof against them and the refutation of their statements; and this verse is among those that were revealed concerning them.

﴿And Allah is Mighty, Owner of Retribution﴾. Al-ʿAziz is the impregnable one who cannot be overcome; from it comes "al-ard al-ʿazzāʾ", the hard ground, which is firm and difficult to traverse. It is also said: al-ʿAziz is the Victorious, whom nothing escapes; from it one says: "man ʿazza bazza", meaning whoever overpowers, plunders. Al-muntaqim is the one who punishes for an offense, and al-niqma is punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah—nothing on the earth or in the heaven is hidden from Him﴾. And this is beyond any doubt.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 6:

﴿He it is who shapes you in the wombs however He wills﴾. This is in refutation of the delegation of Najran, when they said: "Jesus is the son of God." It is as if He is saying: "It is He who fashioned him in the womb, so how could he be a son to Him?!"

It has been related from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "When the drop (nutfah) falls into the womb, it remains a drop for forty days, then a clot ('alaqah) for forty days, then a lump of flesh (mudghah) for forty days. Then Allah, exalted is He, sends an angel who takes dust between his two fingers and mixes it with the lump of flesh. Then he fashions it by the permission of Allah however He (wills): red or black or white, tall or short, handsome or ugly. Then he records its provision, its deeds, its effects, its term of life, and whether it is wretched or happy. Then when it dies, it is buried in the earth from which the dust was taken."

(6) ﴿There is no god but He, the Mighty﴾ in His command, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His dominion.

The Exalted said: ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are decisive (muhkamat), which are the foundation of the Book, and others that are ambiguous (mutashabihat).﴾ The scholars differed regarding the muhkamat and the mutashabihat. Ibn 'Abbas said: The muhkamat are the three verses at the end of Surat al-An'am, which is His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾ up to ﴿These are My straight path, so follow it﴾ [Q. 6:151–153], and His saying ﴿...verses that are decisive, which are the foundation of the Book, and others that are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that which is ambiguous﴾ [Q. 3:7] up to the end of the three verses. As for the mutashabihat, they are the disjointed letters (huruf al-tahajji) at the beginnings of the surahs.

'Ikrimah and Mujahid said: The muhkamat are the lawful and the unlawful, and everything other than that is mutashabih, because some of it resembles the rest in truth and in confirmation, one part confirming another.

Al-Dahhak said: The muhkamat are the nasikh (abrogating verses), and the mutashabihat are the mansukh (abrogated verses).

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari said: The muhkamat are those whose meaning Allah has made known to creation, and the mutashabihat are those whose meaning cannot be understood and which no one knows except Allah. There are two other opinions on this. The first: the muhkamat are those whose meaning is not ambiguous, and the mutashabihat are those whose meaning is ambiguous and unclear. The second: the muhkamat are those which are self-sufficient in meaning, while the mutashabihat are those which are not self-sufficient in meaning except through some form of inference or by being referred to something else. They were called muhkamat from ihkam (making firm), as if He had made them firm, thereby preventing people from altering them, because their meanings are evident and clear.

﴿They are the foundation of the Book﴾ means: they are the origin of the Book. If someone asks: Why did it not say "mothers of the Book" (ummahat al-kitab)? It is said: al-Farra' said: The implied meaning is: they are the thing which is the origin of the Book. Others said: Its meaning is that each one of them is the origin of the Book, as one says: "The people are a lion against me," meaning each one of them is a lion against me. Its meaning is: they are the origin of the Book, because people turn to them for refuge, just as branches turn back to their roots.

If someone asks: How is it that here a distinction is made between the muhkamat and the mutashabihat, while the whole Qur'an is described as mutashabih in His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the most beautiful statement, a Book whose parts resemble one another (mutashabihan)﴾ [Q. 39:23], and the whole is described as muhkam where He says: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm﴾ [Q. 11:1]? We say: When it mentioned "a Book resembling itself" there, it meant that some of it resembles the rest in truth and sincerity. In the other place it mentioned "whose verses have been made firm," meaning that all of it is true and right, with nothing in it that is idle or frivolous. Then He mentioned a further detail after that, making some of it muhkam and some of it mutashabih.

﴿As for those in whose hearts is deviation﴾: Mujahid said: Zaygh is confusion (al-labs). It is said: it is polytheism (shirk). It is also said: it is doubts that attach themselves to the heart. ﴿They follow that which is ambiguous, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation﴾ [Q. 3:7]. This means: those in whose hearts is deviation go to excess in seeking the interpretation of the mutashabih, and so they fall upon a dark interpretation. That is "seeking discord," because whoever goes to excess in religion and seeks the interpretation of what none knows except Allah falls into discord and becomes one who is afflicted. The best of religion is the middle course, in which there is neither excess nor deficiency.

Then they differed about who those are who follow what is ambiguous. It is said: They are the Jews who said: The duration of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) is according to the numerical values of the disjointed letters. It is also said: They are the Christians of the delegation of Najran, when they said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): What do you say about 'Isa? He said: He is the servant of Allah and His messenger. They said: Do you say that he is the word of Allah and a spirit from Him? He said: Yes. They said: Allah is sufficient for us, and they followed what was ambiguous in His saying: "the word of Allah and a spirit from Him." It is also said: They are those who go to excess in seeking the interpretation and following the ambiguous. 'A'ishah related that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse, then said: "When you see those who dispute concerning the verses, beware of them, for they are the ones (meant by Allah)."

His saying the Exalted: ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾. Allah the Exalted has reserved the knowledge of ta'wil (interpretation) to Himself and has cut off the understanding of His servants from it. The difference between ta'wil and tafsir (exegesis) is that tafsir is the mention of the evident meaning, as you say about His saying ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ [Q. 2:2], meaning: there is no doubt in it. As for ta'wil, it is that to which the meaning returns and upon which it settles.

Then there is the discussion of the pause (waqf). Know that Ubayy ibn Ka'b, 'A'ishah and Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of Tawus from him, held the pause to be at the words ﴿except Allah﴾. This is the opinion of al-Hasan and most of the Successors (tabi'un), and al-Kisa'i, al-Farra', al-Akhfash, Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim also said this. They said: The waw in His saying ﴿and those firm in knowledge﴾ is the waw of initiation (waw al-ibtida'). The evidence for its soundness is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas: "and those firm in knowledge say: We believe in it." And Ibn Jurayj related from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, in another narration: the waw is for conjunction (al-nasq), and there is no pause at His saying ﴿except Allah﴾, and that those firm in knowledge know the interpretation. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I am among those who know its interpretation." It is also firmly established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "O Allah, grant him understanding of the religion and teach him the interpretation." They said: The sound (transmission) is the narration of Tawus from Ibn 'Abbas, as we have mentioned, and the consensus of the readers (qurra') is upon it; moreover, the implication of Mujahid's view does not hold.

His saying: ﴿And those firm in knowledge say﴾. The grammarians said: It is only correct to say: "None knows its interpretation except Allah, and those firm in knowledge saying: We believe in it," because He said ﴿those firm in knowledge say: We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord﴾ [Q. 3:7]. Had they known the interpretation, their saying this would have no meaning. It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The Qur'an was revealed in four modes: the lawful and the unlawful, which the Arabs know by their language, what the servants can know of its interpretation, and what none knows the interpretation of except Allah." This supports what we have said. Thus it is established that the pause is at His saying ﴿except Allah﴾, and the waw in His saying ﴿and those firm in knowledge say: We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord﴾ is the waw of initiation. They said: And it is from their firmness in knowledge that they say this. ﴿And none reflects except the people of understanding﴾ [Q. 3:7].

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾, meaning: do not incline our hearts. This is a supplication for steadfastness and for persistence upon it. Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he used to say: "O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." ﴿And grant us from Yourself mercy﴾, meaning support and assistance. ﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, You are gathering the people for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾, meaning: there is no doubt about it according to the people of truth. It was also said: he meant "there is no doubt about it" as the Day of Resurrection, when it comes and becomes manifest.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾. So do not let our hearts deviate, and have mercy upon us. But He was brief and did not mention the completion of the supplication.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 10:

The words of the Most High, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah﴾, are the words of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: "Our wealth and our families preoccupied us from the truth." He says: they have no excuse in this, and that will not benefit them. ﴿And those are the fuel of the Fire﴾.

The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾. Al-da'b: al-sha'n (affair, condition), and al-da'b: al-'adah (habit, custom). The meaning of the verse is that these disbelievers, in denying the Messenger, rejecting the truth, and backing one another in disbelief, are following the custom of the people of Pharaoh. The people of Pharaoh: Pharaoh and his people.

﴿And those before them﴾, meaning: 'Ad and Thamud, ﴿denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins﴾, punished them for their crimes. ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment﴾, because He is everlasting, and His punishment never ceases; and everything everlasting is severe.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: The occasion of the revelation of the verse is what has been related: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished fighting the polytheists on the day of Badr, he gathered the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa' and said to them: 'Embrace Islam before there befalls you what befell the polytheists of the might of Allah.' They said: 'You have met a people who are inexperienced (aghmar) and do not know fighting; had you fought us, you would have seen (that we are different).'" So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed His saying: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting-place.﴾ That is: you will be overcome in this world, and you will be gathered in the Hereafter to Hell, ﴿and wretched is the resting-place﴾.

Muqatil and a group said: It is an address to those polytheists on the day of Badr. Allah says: Say to the polytheists: "You will be overcome, and gathered to Hell," and they were overcome and gathered to Hell. It is also read: "Sayughlabuna wa-yuhsharuna" with the yā' (third person), which has the same meaning as the first. Al-Farra' said: This is like a man saying: "Say to Zayd: 'You are standing,'" which has the same meaning as his saying: "Say to Zayd: 'He is standing'"; the two are equal in meaning.

It may also be that this is an address to the Jews, meaning: Say to those who disbelieve among the Jews: "The polytheists will be overcome, and they will be gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting-place," i.e., wretched is what they have prepared for their own souls, or wretched is what has been prepared for them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There has already been a sign for you﴾, meaning: a miracle and a proof. ﴿In the two hosts that met﴾, meaning: two groups that came together. It is from al-iltiqa' (ملتقى), which is the gathering, and from it comes the phrase "the Day of Meeting" (يوم التلاق), because on it the people of the heavens and the people of the earth gather. ﴿One group fighting in the way of Allah﴾, meaning the Muslims on the Day of Badr, ﴿and another disbelieving﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿seeing them as twice their number with the eye of sight﴾, meaning the Muslims saw the polytheists as twice their number, when in fact they were three times their number. This is because the number of Muslims on the Day of Badr was three hundred and thirteen men, or fourteen men, and the number of the polytheists was nine hundred and fifty. ﴿Allah supports with His help whom He wills. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those of vision﴾.

It is also narrated from Ali and Ibn Mas'ud that the number of the polytheists was a thousand, and the Muslims saw them as a little over six hundred. Ibn Mas'ud said: "We saw them as twice our number, then we saw them as equal to our number, man for man." This is the meaning of the saying of Allah, exalted is He, in Surah al-Anfal: ﴿And when He showed them to you when you met, in your eyes as few, and He made you few in their eyes, that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed﴾. So the Muslims saw them fewer than their actual number, and likewise the polytheists saw the Muslims fewer than their actual number. The wisdom in this was that when they saw them as fewer than they were, they did not shrink back and did not slacken in fighting, because Allah, exalted is He, had informed them that one of them would confront two of the polytheists. Likewise, when the polytheists saw the Muslims as fewer than they were, they did not refrain from fighting; ﴿that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed﴾, and that was the killing of their leaders and commanders, by the permission of Allah, exalted is He.

Al-Farra' said: "They saw them in their actual number as they were, and His saying ﴿seeing them as twice their number﴾ means twice their number besides their own number, similar to the saying of a man who has a dirham and says: 'I need twice this dirham,' meaning twice it in addition to itself." The first view is more correct.

It has also been read as "tarawnahum" (ترونهم) with the letter ta', in which case it is addressed to the Jews, for a group of them had attended the fighting at Badr to see which side would prevail. They saw the polytheists as twice the number of the Muslims, and they saw the help was nevertheless for the Muslims, and that was a miracle and a sign for the Messenger (ﷺ) in their eyes. According to the first reading, the address is with the Muslims in His saying: ﴿There has already been a sign for you in the two hosts that met; and Allah supports with His help whom He wills﴾, because it was the Muslims who were helped on that day.

﴿Indeed, in that is a lesson for those of insight﴾, meaning: a sign for those of insight in religion and for all people of intellect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Adorned for people is the love of desires: women, children,﴾ Al-Hasan said: The one who adorns is Satan, because Allah, exalted is He, censured the world with the most eloquent censure, so He would not make it appealing in people's eyes. The common body of exegetes said: The one who adorns is Allah, exalted is He, and His adornment is that He made the desire for women and children beloved in their hearts, ﴿and the heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾. So "qanatir" (heaped amounts) is the plural of "qintar" (a quintal), which is a great amount of wealth. Then they differed. Mu'adh and Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: a qintar is one thousand two hundred ounces. Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: it is one thousand dinars, or twelve thousand dirhams. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: it is eighty thousand dirhams. Mujahid said: it is seventy thousand dinars. Qatadah said: it is one hundred ratls of gold or silver. Abu Nadrah said: it is the filling of an ox-hide of gold or silver. It was named "qintar" from "ihkam" (securing) and "tawthiq" (binding). As for "muqantarah" (heaped up), it is the collected and piled up. Al-Farra' said: the qanatir are three, and the muqantarah are nine.

His saying: ﴿And the branded horses﴾. Mujahid said: they are the fine, well-formed ones. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-musawwamah (the branded or pastured ones) means the grazing ones; it is said: "asama al-khayl" (he pastured the horses) from grazing. There is a third view: al-musawwamah means those marked with a sign, from "al-sima", which is the mark. Some said: its sima is resemblance, and some said: its sima is branding. ﴿And the cattle﴾: these are camels, cows and sheep. ﴿And the tilled land﴾: these are the lands prepared for cultivation. ﴿That is the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾: in it is an indication that it is an enjoyment that perishes.

﴿And with Allah is the best return﴾: in it is a discouragement from the world and an encouragement toward the Hereafter. Then He emphasized it.

By His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who are mindful of Allah, with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah.﴾ It is recited (qira'ah) as "ridwān" with a damma on the rā', and both forms have the same meaning. It is said: "radiya yarḍā riḍā'an wa riḍwānan" (he was pleased, he is pleased, with pleasure and approval). And in a report from the Prophet (ﷺ): "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, Allah, Exalted is He, says: 'Indeed, I have a promise for you, and I will fulfil it for you.' They say: 'Have You not given us what we hoped for? What is it, O Lord?' He says: 'I will let My pleasure (riḍwān) descend upon you, and I will never be displeased with you again.'"

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of the servants, those who say﴾

So the phrase ﴿Those who say﴾ (al-ladhina yaqulun) may be in the genitive position (majrur), in which case the implied sense is: "[of] the servants who say." It may also be in the nominative position (marfu'), with the implied sense: "They say," as a new sentence (mubtada'). And it may be in the accusative position (mansub), with the implied sense: "I mean: those who say:" ﴿Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.﴾

﴿The patient﴾ may be in the genitive case (*khafḍ*, the grammatical case of the genitive), and it may be in the accusative case (*naṣb*, the grammatical case of the accusative). It means: those who are patient in the face of hardships and calamities, patient in acts of obedience, and patient in refraining from sins. ﴿And the truthful﴾: those whose states and actions are upright. ﴿And the devout﴾: those who persist in obedience and are constant in it. ﴿And the spenders﴾ means: those who give charity. It was said that this refers to spending in jihad, and it was said that it refers to all forms of goodness. ﴿And those who seek forgiveness at dawn﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they are those who pray at night. Anas said: they are those who ask for forgiveness. Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are those who pray the dawn prayer in congregation. He restricted it to ﴿at dawn﴾ only because the dawn prayer is close to the time of *saḥar* (the last part of the night before dawn).

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 3, verse 18:

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿God bears witness﴾ means: He makes clear and makes known. Every witness is one who makes clear and makes known. ﴿that there is no god but He﴾ by Himself, in His oneness. This is because the delegation of Najran had denied His oneness, and this verse is one of the verses revealed concerning them, as a proof against them. ﴿And the angels﴾ means: the angels also bear witness. ﴿And those of knowledge﴾ It is said that they are the scholars of the Children of Israel, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and those who believed with him. It is also said that they are the Muhajirun (emigrants) and the Ansar (helpers). It is also said that they are all the scholars of the Ummah.

﴿Standing firm in justice﴾ is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative), so He, the Exalted, is the One who stands in charge of the management of creation. ﴿In justice﴾: with equity (al-qist). It is said: qasata yaqsutu when he acted unjustly, and aqsata yuqsitu when he acted justly. So al-qasit is the unjust one, and from this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿As for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell﴾. Al-muqsit is the just one, and from this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who act justly﴾. ﴿There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 19:

﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam.﴾ It is also read "Anna al-din" with the alif opened (fath). Whoever reads it with the alif kasra (kasr) takes it as a fresh beginning (ibtida'). Al-Kisa'i read it with the accusative (nasb), and its implied sense is: "Allah bears witness that the religion with Allah is Islam; there is no god except Him." Islam (al-islam) is submission and surrender (al-inqiyad wa al-istislam). Bare submission without belief may also be called islam, to distinguish it from iman (faith), as will come later.

Islam as known in the sharia is: bringing the two testimonies (al-shahadatayn) together with the rest of the five pillars. In the traditions it is reported that deeds will be brought on the Day of Resurrection. Prayer (salat) will be brought in a form, and it will say: "O Lord, I am the prayer." Allah the Exalted will say: "You are good." Zakat will be brought in a form, and it will say: "O Lord, I am the zakat." Allah will say: "You are good." It is the same with fasting and the pilgrimage (hajj). Then Islam will be brought in the most beautiful of forms, and it will say: "O Lord, I am Islam." Allah the Exalted will say: "You are on the way to good. Through you I take and through you I give today."

It is related from Ghalib al-Qattan that he said: "I came to Kufa for trade and lodged near al-A'mash. I used to frequent him and hear hadith from him. One night I intended to set off from him toward Basra, and I found him worshipping intensively in the mosque. He passed by this verse: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those possessing knowledge, standing in justice; there is no god except Him, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Then he said: 'And I bear witness to what Allah has borne witness to, and I entrust Allah with this testimony, so that it may be a deposit with Him for me.' Then he said: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam,﴾ repeating it several times. I said to myself: 'He has heard something in it.' He stayed, and I prayed the dawn prayer with him. Then I said to him: 'I passed by this verse, and you were repeating it.' He said: 'Has it not reached you what has been narrated about it?'

I said: 'I have been with you for two years and you have not related to me [anything], and I intended to set off toward Basra.' He said: 'By Allah, I will not narrate to you for a year.' So I remained in Kufa and wrote on his door that day. When the year was complete I came to him and said: 'O Abu Muhammad, the year is complete.' He said: 'Abu Wa'il narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "A person will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah the Exalted will say: 'This servant of Mine had a covenant with Me, and I am most worthy of fulfilling the covenant. Admit My servant into Paradise.'"'

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who were given the Book did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves.﴾ That is: the Jews and the Christians. "Baghyan baynahum" means: out of envy among them. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 20:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if they argue with you﴾, meaning: if they dispute with you, ﴿then say, "I have submitted my face to God, and so have those who follow me"﴾, meaning: I have directed my worship to God, Exalted is He. ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture﴾, meaning: the Jews and the Christians, ﴿and to the unlettered ones (al-ummiyyin)﴾, meaning: the polytheists.

﴿Have you submitted?﴾ meaning: submit! It is said that it is phrased as a threat, as one says, "Will you accept this from me?" in the sense of a threat. ﴿If they submit, then they have been guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance (al-balagh) [of the message], and God is Seeing of the servants﴾, meaning: upon you is the conveying of the message, and upon you is not the guidance (al-hidayah), ﴿and God is Seeing of the servants﴾, regarding the one who strays among them and the one who is guided.

The summary of the meaning of the verse: God, Exalted is He, says: "If they argue with you in falsehood, then say: I have submitted my face to God," that is, I have sincerely devoted my action to God, or I have directed my worship to God, the One whom you do not acknowledge as the Creator and Sustainer. For they were acknowledging that God is their Creator and Sustainer. So I direct my worship to Him, and I do not follow my desires as you follow your desires.

Then He said: ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered ones, "Have you submitted?"﴾, meaning: submit! Just as He said: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾, meaning: desist! The polytheists were called unlettered (ummiyyin) because they were not readers (of the Scripture). It is also said that they were attributed to Umm al-Qura, which is Makkah, because they dwelt there.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 21:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾ He means by this the Jews, the children of Israel. ﴿And kill the prophets without right﴾. He only said "without right" for emphasis, because the killing of the prophets cannot be divided into what is right and what is wrong.

Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who kill a prophet, or whom a prophet kills." Then he narrated in this report that he said: "The Children of Israel killed forty-two prophets in a single hour. Then there rose up to them one hundred and twelve men from their ascetics and worshippers, and they enjoined what is good, and they [the killers] killed them." This is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿and kill those who enjoin justice from among the people﴾, i.e., with equity. ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ He addressed their descendants with this, although the crime was committed by their forefathers, because they (the descendants) approved of their deeds and adhered to their religion, and so they deserved this punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become void﴾, i.e., they have been nullified. Ḥubūṭ (nullification, coming to nothing) and buṭlān (invalidation) apply both in this world and in the Hereafter. The nullification of deeds in this world means that they are not accepted; in the Hereafter it means that they are not rewarded with reward. ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾, i.e., no one who will prevent the punishment from them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 23:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ It has been said: this was revealed concerning the Jews of the tribes of Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir. For the Prophet (ﷺ) came to the house of their study (madaris), and Nu'aym ibn 'Amr and al-Harith ibn Yazid said to him: "Upon which religion are you?" He said: "Upon the religion of Ibrahim." Nu'aym said: "Ibrahim was a Jew." He said: "Between me and you is the Torah; bring out the Torah." But they refused to bring it out. This is the meaning of His words ﴿they are invited to the Book of Allah, that it may judge between them﴾, i.e., the Torah.

There is another view concerning this: that the verse was revealed concerning the Christians of the delegation of Najran, and His words ﴿they are invited to the Book of Allah﴾ refer to the Qur'an, that it may judge between them.

﴿Then a faction of them turn away, while they are averse﴾. This is because some of them had embraced Islam.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days."﴾ This refers to the Jews, and we have mentioned it before. ﴿And their fabrications in their religion deceived them.﴾ Al-ghurur (deception) is enticing someone with what yields nothing from it. Al-ghurur also means the Devil. Gharra al-thawb means folding the garment; it is said, "Return the garment to its fold (ghurr)," meaning to its folded state. Al-ghurur also means taking a risk. ﴿What they used to fabricate.﴾ Al-iftira' (fabrication) is inventing falsehood; from it comes al-firya (calumny), which is the arranging of falsehood. The poet said:

(And you do not fabricate what you have created... while some people create and then do not fabricate)

That is: he does not lie and does not arrange (falsehood).

"His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿How then, when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul is paid in full what it has earned﴾ — i.e., how then will their condition be — ﴿when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul is paid in full what it has earned, of recompense, while they will not be wronged﴾."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 26:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty﴾. Regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse there are two reports. The first: when he (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he promised his Companions the kingdom of Persia. The Jews heard this and said: "Far-fetched! Persia and Rome are mightier and more secure in their domains than you imagine." So this verse was revealed.

Al-Hasan said: he asked his Lord, on behalf of his Companions, for the kingdom of Persia and Rome.

As for his saying ﴿Say: O Allah﴾, its origin is "Yā Allāh" (O Allah). When the vocative particle was removed, the letter mim was added at its end. Al-Farra' said: the mim in it carries a meaning, and its meaning is "O Allah, help us with forgiveness," i.e., "Direct us (aqsidna)."

﴿Owner of sovereignty﴾: its estimated form is "O Owner of sovereignty." Its meaning: the owner of the servants and of what they possess. It was also said: by "sovereignty" is meant prophethood. It was also said: the owner of the heavens and the earth. ﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾, i.e., to whom You will to give it among the Muslims. ﴿And You strip sovereignty from whom You will﴾, i.e., from whom You will to strip it, and they are Persia and Rome. ﴿You exalt whom You will and You abase whom You will﴾: there are three opinions regarding this. The first: You exalt whom You will with victory, and abase whom You will with subjugation. The second: You exalt whom You will with wealth, and abase whom You will with poverty. The third: You exalt whom You will with guidance, and abase whom You will with misguidance.

﴿In Your hand is the good﴾, i.e., in Your hand is the good and the evil, as He said: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾, i.e., protect you from the heat and the cold, so one of the two mentioned is sufficient in place of the other.

﴿Indeed You are over all things competent﴾. Regarding the virtue of this verse, reports have come: what was related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his father, from Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Al-Fatihah, Ayat al-Kursi, and two verses from Al 'Imran (Shahida Allah, and this verse) are intercessors for the one who recites them on the Day of Resurrection; there is no barrier between them and Allah." It was also reported in this report that he said: "When Allah the Exalted revealed these verses, they clung to the Throne and said: 'O Lord, will You send us down to Your earth and Your servants?' Allah the Exalted said: 'By My might and My majesty, no servant of Mine recites you except that I will settle him in My Paradise, in the state he was in, and I will fulfil for him seventy needs every day, the least of which is forgiveness.'"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 27:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿You cause the night to enter into the day, and You cause the day to enter into the night﴾. Al-iylaj (causing to enter) means al-idkhal (making enter), and its meaning is: You diminish one of them and increase the other. It was also said that its meaning is: You cover the night with the day, and the day with the night.

﴿And You bring forth the living from the dead, and You bring forth the dead from the living﴾. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: You bring forth the disbeliever from the believer, and the believer from the disbeliever. The second opinion: You bring forth the drop of semen from the living, and the living from the drop of semen. There is also a rare opinion in this: You bring forth the intelligent, shrewd person from the foolish sinner, and the foolish from the intelligent; for the foolish one is dead in understanding, and the intelligent one is alive in understanding.

The word ﴿mayyit﴾ (dead) is recited both with light and with heavy emphasis (mayyit and mayyit). The grammarians of Kufa distinguished between mayyit and mayyit, saying: mayyit (with the shadda) is one who is living but will not die, and mayyit (with light pronunciation) is one who has died. They cited the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾. The grammarians of Basra rejected this and said: the two have one and the same meaning.

Al-Mubarrad recited for one of the poets:

(He who has died and found rest is not a dead one; the dead one is rather the dead among the living.)

(The dead one is only he who lives in misery, with downcast heart, having little hope.)

Thus he combined mayyit and mayyit with one meaning.

﴿And You provide for whom You will without reckoning﴾: without restriction or stinginess.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 28:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾. This was addressed to specific people who had become Muslim while still maintaining allegiance (muwalah) to the Jews and the polytheists, so Allah forbade them from that. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾.

﴿And whoever does that has nothing with Allah﴾, meaning: he is not of the party of Allah. ﴿Except when you fear a danger from them﴾. It has also been recited as taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation), and the two have the same meaning, meaning: except when one falls into their hands and fears them, so he conforms to them with his tongue while his heart is content with faith. There is no blame on him for that. But if he endures patiently until he is killed, he will have a great reward, ﴿and Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾.

It has been narrated: "Musaylimah the liar, may Allah curse him, seized two men from the companions of the Messenger of Allah and said to one of them: 'Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes,' out of taqiyyah. So he released him. Then he said to the other: 'Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, yes, yes.' He said: 'Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'I am deaf,' so he killed him. This reached the Messenger of Allah, and he mentioned the rank of the one who endured patiently until he was killed, and said: 'As for the first, he took the concession of Allah.'"

It has been authentically related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The best jihad is a word of truth before an oppressive ruler." And he said: "The most excellent of martyrs after the martyrs of Uhud is one who stands before an oppressive ruler, commands him to do good, and forbids him from evil, and so he is killed for it."

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾, meaning: He causes you to fear Him. ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾, meaning: the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it﴾, that is: He will recompense for it. ﴿And He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah is over all things Competent﴾. The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present (before it)﴾. That is: there will be presented to it what it has done of good and evil, so it will rejoice in what it did of good.

﴿And what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that there were a far-distant term﴾. That is: an extended, lengthy limit. Al-Suddi said: the distance between the East and the West. And it is reported in the traditions (akhbar) that deeds will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in forms: whatever was good will be in a good form, and whatever was evil will be in an ugly form.

﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants﴾. From His kindness is that He warned them, encouraged them and frightened them, and promised them and threatened them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾. Regarding the occasion of the revelation of this verse there are two opinions.

The first: it is addressed to the Jews and Christians of the delegation of Najran. They said: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones," so there was revealed His saying: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾.

The second: it is addressed to the polytheists of Quraysh. He saw them worshipping idols, so he said to them: "You have opposed the religion (millah) of your father Abraham." They said: "We only worship them to draw near to Allah, for we love Him." So there was revealed His saying, exalted is He: {Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful}.

Know that the love of Allah for the servant, and the love of the servant for Allah, does not occur through the pleasure of desire. Rather, the servant's love in regard to Allah is coming to obey Him, seeking His pleasure, and following His command. The love of Allah in regard to the servant is His pardon of him, His forgiveness, and good praise; and He confirmed it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 32:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾. He made clear that His love is in obedience to Him and obedience to His Messenger.

﴿But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾. If someone asks: why did he repeat the name of Allah several times, when it would have sufficed for him to say "indeed He does not love the disbelievers"? It is said: this is in accordance with the custom of the Arabs, for it is among their habits that when they magnify something, they repeat its mention. Sibawayh recited, as an example of this, the verse:

(I do not see death as anything that preceded death... the death of the rich and the poor has troubled it)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 33:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah﴾. Al-istifa' (choosing, selecting): al-ikhtiyar (choice). And al-safwa: al-khiyara (the choice part, the best). And why did He choose Adam? They differed. Among them were those who said: He chose him for the religion (al-din), and among them were those who said: He chose him for prophethood (al-nubuwwa). If someone says: To whom was he sent? It is said: To the angels, to the extent that he taught them the names, and to his offspring. He said: The family of Abraham are Ishmael, Isaac and Jacob.

And the family of Imran: Moses and Aaron. The family of Imran is from the family of Abraham. It was also said: He meant by it Jesus, since he is the son of Mary, daughter of Imran. ﴿Over the worlds﴾: over the worlds of the people of their time.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Offspring, one of another﴾. It was said: it is derived from dhara'a (ذرأ) meaning "to create." It was also said: it is from al-dharr (الذر, the tiny particles/ants), because He created them and brought them out of the loins of Adam like dharr. The sons are called dhurriyya (ذُرِّيَّة, offspring), and likewise the fathers. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾, meaning their fathers. The sons are dhurriyya because He created them (dhara'a), and the fathers are dhurriyya because He created the sons from them. (One of another) in terms of excellence; and it was said: in terms of procreation. ﴿And God is All-Hearing﴾ of what they say, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what they conceal.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When the wife of 'Imran said﴾, and she is Hannah, the wife of 'Imran, and her sister was under Zakariyya. ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as dedicated (muharraran)﴾. Al-Sha'bi said: its meaning is devoted sincerely to the worship of Allah, the Exalted. Mujahid said: its meaning is designated for service of the House, free for it from all other occupations. ﴿So accept it from me; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. The meaning is apparent."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 36:

The words of His Exalted saying: ﴿So when she gave birth to her, she said, "My Lord, I have given birth to a female"﴾. This was because her husband, ʿImran, had rebuked her (ʿatabaha) for what she had vowed, and he said to her: "You do not know whether your child will be male or female, and you had vowed unconditionally."

﴿And Allah knew best what she had given birth to﴾. This is a report from Allah, the Exalted, about His knowledge. It is also read as "And Allah knew best what she had given birth to" in the indicative mood, and this is part of the woman's speech: ﴿and the male is not like the female﴾. The male is more fit and stronger for serving the place of worship (bi'ah) than the female. It was also said: because he is further from the impediments to worship, unlike the female, whom menstruation and postnatal bleeding (nifas) prevent.

﴿And I have named her Maryam﴾. If someone says: what is the meaning of her saying, "And I have named her Maryam"? It is said: so that it might be known whether that name was given with the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted, so that it might be changed or confirmed.

﴿And her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and made her grow in a good growth, and entrusted her to Zakariyya. Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the sanctuary (mihrab), he found with her provision. He said﴾.

﴿And I seek refuge for her in You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Satan﴾. Thus, al-Shaytan means the one who is driven away, and al-Rajim means the one who is stoned with meteors. Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no child born but that Satan pokes him in his side, so he begins to cry out, except Maryam and her son, for he struck them, but the blow fell upon the veil." And he recited the words of the Exalted: ﴿And I seek refuge for her in You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Satan﴾.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 37:**

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Then her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance﴾, meaning: He was pleased with her and accepted her. ﴿And caused her to grow with a good growth﴾, meaning: He caused her to grow, and so she grew with a good growth.

Abu al-'Abbas ibn 'Ata al-Sufi said: When God caused her to grow with a good growth, look at its fruit, how the plant bore fruit. He means 'Isa, may God's blessings be upon him.

﴿And he made Zakariyya her guardian﴾, read with a shadda on the kaf (*kaffala*), and it is also read without shadda, *kafala*, with a damma on the alif. The meaning of *kafala* (guardianship, taking responsibility) is "to take in," meaning Zakariyya took her into his own care. Whoever reads with the shadda, its meaning is that God placed her under Zakariyya's guardianship. The Prophet said: "I and the one who sponsors an orphan are like these two," (ﷺ).

Among the reasons Zakariyya was singled out for the guardianship of Maryam is that her maternal aunt was married to him, and she was the sister of Hannah, the wife of 'Imran. The story of Zakariyya's guardianship of Maryam is well known and will come in Surah Maryam, God willing.

﴿Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab﴾. "Zakariyya" is read with both the long and the short vowel. The *mihrab* (a private upper chamber or sanctuary, reached by a ladder) was a room one ascended to by a ladder, and Zakariyya had made for Maryam a room like that, and he would climb up to it by a ladder. A poet said regarding this:

*(Mistress of the chamber, when I came to her, I did not reach her unless I climbed up a ladder.)*

That is, a mistress of a chamber. It is also said that the *mihrab* is the most noble of assemblies. It is also said that it is the well-known prayer niche.

﴿He found with her provision﴾. *Rizq* (provision) is what is eaten. Qatada said: Winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter. He had seen it with her. Al-Hasan said: When Maryam was born, she did not take the breast, and God would bring her provision.

﴿He said, "O Maryam, from where is this for you?"﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: its meaning is "from where is this for you?" The grammarians rejected this and said: this is a laxity on the part of Abu 'Ubayda, because there is a difference between them: *anna* (أَنى) is used to ask about the direction (from what source or by what way), and *ayna* (أَيْن) is used to ask about the place. Al-Mubarrad recited a line of verse by one of them, illustrating the difference between them:

*(Anna and min ayna, whence has this joyful excitement come upon you?)*

His words, ﴿Anni laka hadha?﴾ mean: from what direction is this for you?

﴿She said, "It is from God. Indeed God provides for whom He wills without account."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There Zakariyya prayed to his Lord﴾. This is because Zakariyya, when he saw Maryam receiving her provision out of its season, such as summer fruit in winter, was filled with hope that a child might be granted to him out of its season, in old age. So he prayed to God that He would grant him a son. He had reached one hundred and twenty years of age, and his wife had reached ninety-eight years.

﴿He said: "My Lord, grant me from Yourself﴾ (from You) ﴿a good offspring﴾, that is, a righteous, pious and pure son. The word offspring (dhurriyyah) includes both male and female. He said ﴿good﴾ in the feminine form, agreeing with the wording of the word offspring (dhurriyyah), which is feminine. ﴿Then the angels called to him, while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "God gives you glad tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from God﴾ (dhurriyyah is a feminine noun here).

﴿Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 39:

﴿Then the angels called to him﴾, and it is also read: "fanadahu al-mala'ikah" (with an alif). They differed regarding the one who called out. Some said: it was Jibril (Gabriel). Others said: it was a group of the angels. ﴿while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings"﴾. "Anna" is read with a kasra on the alif and with a fatha. Whoever reads it with a kasra, its implied sense is: "the angels called to him and said: Indeed Allah gives you good tidings." Whoever reads it with a fatha, it is in the same construction (al-nasq). ﴿yubashshiruka﴾ is read both lightened and doubled, and both have the same meaning.

Al-bushara (good tidings) is a pleasing news whose effect appears on the surface of the face. ﴿Gives you good tidings of Yahya﴾: he named him Yahya before he was born. ﴿Confirming a word from Allah﴾. It was said: confirming a Book of Allah and His speech. It was also said: its meaning is confirming Isa, who is "the word of Allah." If someone says: "the word of Allah" cannot be a created thing, and we have denied the Christians their saying "the Messiah is the son of Allah" and their saying "Allah is the third of three," so how do we know that Isa is the word of Allah? It is said: there are three opinions concerning this.

The first: he is the word of Allah in the sense that he came into being by a word from Allah, when He said to him "Be," and he was, without cause or reason, and without the act of a human or the casting of a drop of semen.

The second: he is the word of Allah in the sense that he is guided by it, just as one is guided by the speech of Allah.

The third: Allah, exalted is He, had informed all the prophets and promised them in His books that He would create a prophet without a father, and He promised Maryam that a child would be born to her without a father. When Isa came into being, He called him a word, because he came about through that word and that promise. This is like the Arabs saying: "Recite to me your kalima," meaning your qasida (poem). It was said to Hassan: "Al-Hawdira composed a qasida," and he said: "May Allah curse his kalima," meaning his qasida. Since the qasida came into being through his word, it was called a kalima.

His saying: ﴿and a master, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous﴾. As for al-sayyid (master): Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-sayyid is the pious. Mujahid said: he is the generous. It was said: he is the forbearing who is not provoked by anything. It was said: he is the one who surpasses his people in all qualities of goodness.

Al-hasur (chaste): Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' and a group said: he is the one who does not approach women. Al-hasur is in the sense of al-mahsur (the one restrained), and he was prevented from women. It is like the saying of the poet:

(In it are forty-two milking-camels, black like the dark feather of the glossy raven.)

So "halubah" (milch-camel) means "mahlub" (milked). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: he had something like the fold of a garment (a small piece of skin, i.e. he had no genital organ in the normal sense), and he married nonetheless so that he would lower his gaze. Al-Sha'bi said: al-hasur is the impotent (al-'anin). There is another opinion: al-hasur is the one who refrains from intercourse while being able to perform it, and this agrees with the opinion of al-Shafi'i in the matter of withdrawing for the worship of Allah.

They chose this view for two reasons. First: it is closer to deserving praise, since the statement came in the form of praise. Second: it keeps further from attributing a defect to the prophets, since they are far from defects.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has already overtaken me and my wife is barren?"﴾ He said "old age has already overtaken me" (balaghani al-kibar) because old age is something a person seeks (fi talab al-insan), so when it reaches him, it has overtaken him.

As for al-'aqir (the barren woman), she is the one whose womb has become sterile due to old age. If it is said: he was doubtful about God's promise when he said, ﴿My Lord, how can I have a son?﴾ it is answered: he said it by way of humility (ʿalā sabīl al-tawāḍuʿ), meaning: a man in my state of old age, to have a child from a woman like this old woman, is that possible? It is also said that its meaning is: how can this boy be mine? Will You return me to the state of youth, or will the boy come into being while I am in the state of old age?

﴿He said: "Thus does God do what He wills."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿My Lord, appoint for me a sign.﴾ That is: a sign (ʿalāma). It has been said: He only asked for a sign because Iblis had whispered to him that the one who called you was the devil and not an angel, and he kept persisting in this whispering. So he asked for a sign to repel that whispering. It has also been said: he only asked for a sign in order to know the time of the birth, so that he might increase in thanks to God.

﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days.﴾ It has been said: [God] restrained his tongue and withheld speech from him for three days. This is a sound opinion, and it is what the saying of the Exalted in Surah Maryam indicates: ﴿Three nights, sound.﴾

﴿Except by gesture (ramz).﴾ That is: a sign (ishāra). Signing may be done with the tongue, with the hand, or with the eye. What is meant here is signing with the extended index finger. Qatadah said: He only restrained his tongue from speech as a punishment for him, because of what he asked regarding the sign after God had revealed to him, and after the angels had addressed him with the good news.

﴿And remember your Lord much, and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning.﴾ It has been said: He only restrained his tongue from speaking with people, and did not restrain it from remembrance of God, so He commanded him to remember. The word for glorification (tasbīh) here means prayer (ṣalāt). As for al-ʿashī (the evening), it is the period between the decline of the sun and its setting, and from it come the prayers of Dhuhr and ʿAṣr, called "the two evening prayers." As for al-ibkār (the morning), it is the period from the break of dawn until the high forenoon (ḍuḥā).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 42:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And when the angels said, "O Mary"﴾ meaning: and remember when the angels said: ﴿"O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you"﴾ He chose you and purified you from menstruation (hayd) and postnatal bleeding (nifas). It is also said: from sins. ﴿"And purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds"﴾. Some said: above the women of the worlds of her time, and some said: above (all the women of) the worlds, in that she gave birth without a father, and this was not granted to any woman of the worlds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾, meaning: obey your Lord, and stand up to His obedience. Qunut (devout obedience; prolonged standing) is prolonged standing. Mujahid said: its meaning is, prolong your standing before your Lord. It has also been said: she stood until her feet swelled and became puffy. Qunut in prayer was so named because it is performed in the state of standing. And it is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he was asked about the best prayer, and he said: "Prolonged qunut," meaning: prolonged standing.

﴿And prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow﴾. It has been said: prostration was mentioned before bowing only because it was so in their law (shari'ah). It has also been said otherwise: rather, bowing comes before prostration in all the sacred laws, and the conjunction "wa" (and) does not indicate sequence but mere combination. A man may say, "I saw Zayd and 'Amr," even if he saw 'Amr before Zayd, and one may say, "I saw 'Amr and Zayd," meaning Zayd and 'Amr. The poet said:

(Ala ya nakhlata min dhati 'irq ... 'alayki wa rahmatu Allahi as-salam)

meaning: upon you be peace and the mercy of God. Likewise His saying: ﴿prostrate yourself and bow﴾ means: bow and prostrate yourself. He said "with those who bow" and did not say "with those women who bow," so that it would be more general and comprehensive. It has also been said that its meaning is: with those who pray in congregation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 44:

Allah's statement: ﴿That is among the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you﴾. He says to Muhammad: That is among the reports of the unseen which We reveal to you. ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens (aqlam), [to see] which of them would take charge of Maryam, and you were not with them when they disputed﴾. So "al-aqlam" means the arrows (al-sihham), and it was called qalam (pen) only because it cuts and is trimmed (yuqta' wa yubra). The root meaning of qalam is cutting, and from it comes qalam al-zifr (the nail-paring).

The story concerning this is that they quarrelled and disputed over the guardianship (kafalah) of Maryam. Zakariyya said: "I have more right to her guardianship than you, because her maternal aunt is with me." Their rabbis (ahbaruhum), and it was said their guardians (awliya'uhum), said: "We have more right to her guardianship, because her father was our imam and our rabbi." So they drew lots (faqtara'u) and cast arrows (istahamu), on the condition that whoever's pen remained in the water and rose up would be the one with the right to her guardianship. So they cast their pens onto the water, each pen bearing the name of one of them. Their pens sank and flowed along in the water, while the pen of Zakariyya moved upward against the current to the surface of the water. It was said: their pens were submerged, and Zakariyya's pen turned back and remained above the water. It was also said: they disputed over her guardianship because a famine and hardship had befallen them, and the expense had become burdensome for them; so they cast lots for her guardianship, pushing one another, until whoever's arrow came out would be the one who supports her and spends on her. The first account is more sound and more well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 45:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When the angels said: "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good news of a word from Him"﴾. It is said: the angels spoke these words to her directly and face to face (mushafahah wa 'iyanan).

﴿His name will be the Messiah (al-Masih), Jesus, son of Mary﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he was only named Masih because he did not pass his hand over anyone afflicted with a defect except that he was healed. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: he was named Masih because he was anointed with blessing (masah bil-barakah). It is also said: al-Masih means al-siddiq (the truthful one), and al-Masih may also mean al-kadhdhab (the liar), and this is one of the words with opposite meanings (min al-adhdad). It is also said: he was named Masih because he would wipe over the face of the earth (yamsah wajh al-ard) and travel through it (yasih fiha). It is also said: he was only named Masih because he had a smooth sole, with no hollow in the soles of his feet (mamsuh al-qadam li-akhmas qadamayh). From this is the saying of the poet:

(He spent the night measuring it, a youth like an arrow-shaft, thin-shinned, smooth-soled.)

From this also, al-Dajjal was named Masih, because one side of his face was wiped out, having no eye.

﴿Honoured in this world and the Hereafter﴾, that is: exalted, having high standing (jah) with Allah. (﴿And of those brought near﴾)

Wa-yukallimu al-nasa fi al-mahdi wa-kahlan wa-min al-salihin (and he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous).

As for his speaking in the cradle, it is his saying in Surah Maryam: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah﴾. The Christians deny his speaking in the cradle, and its explanation will come later. As for his speaking while he is a kahl (a man in middle age), it is said: it is his informing about the miraculous matters. And it is said: it is his speech after his descent from the heaven.

Al-kahl: it is said that he is one who is above the ghulam (youth) and below the shaykh (elder), and he is thirty-four years old. Its origin is: height/tallness, and from it: iktahala al-nabat (the plants grew tall and matured) when it grew tall.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 47:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿She said: My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?﴾ She said this in wonder, since the custom had not been that a child should be born without a father. ﴿He said: So it is. Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be, and it is.﴾ That is, nothing is difficult for Him; He does what He wills and judges as He desires.

Almost every term here is a Qur'anic quotation or a technical gloss, so I'll translate as instructed.

The Words of the Exalted: ﴿And He will teach him the Book﴾. It is read with the yā' (ya-) and the nūn (na-) [i.e., yu'allimuhu, "He will teach him" / "We will teach him"]. "Al-Kitāb" means the writing (al-khatt). ﴿And the wisdom﴾: this means knowledge (al-'ilm) and understanding (al-fiqh). ﴿And the Torah and the Gospel﴾: Allah taught him the Torah and the Gospel.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 49:

﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel.﴾ Some of them said: he was a messenger while still in childhood (sabā'). Others said: he was only made a messenger after reaching maturity (bulūgh).

﴿That I have certainly come to you with a sign from your Lord.﴾ Its meaning: with signs from your Lord. He mentioned only "a sign" (āyah) because all of them point to one thing.

﴿That I create for you from clay [something] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by the permission of Allah.﴾ That is, I determine and shape. It was said: Jesus said to them, "What is the strongest of creatures in creation?" They said, "The bat." So he shaped from clay a bat, fashioned it, and breathed into it, and it began to fly by the permission of Allah.

(﴿from your Lord, that I create for you from clay [something] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by the permission of Allah, and I heal the one born blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah, and I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses.﴾ And I heal the one born blind.) Abū ʿUbayd said: the akmah (the one born blind) is the one who was born blind. It was also said: it is the aʿmash (one with weak sight) who sees by day but not by night. ﴿And the leper﴾: the one who has baraṣ (white patches on the skin). ﴿And I bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbās said: he brought four to life: ʿĀzar, the son of the old woman, the daughter of the tax-collector (al-ʿāshir), and Sām ibn Nūḥ, upon him be peace.

As for ʿĀzar, he was a friend of Jesus, and he was informed of his death, so he called upon Allah, the Exalted, and He brought him back to life. As for the son of the old woman, he was on a bier being carried to the graveyard, and Jesus saw him, so he ordered the bier to be set down, and he called upon Allah and he came back to life; he took off his shroud, put on his clothes, and returned to the house. As for the daughter of the tax-collector, a man who used to collect tithes had a daughter who died, so he called upon Allah and she was brought back to life. As for Sām ibn Nūḥ, Jesus came to his grave and called upon Allah, and he came back to life. He rose up to him and said, "Has the Resurrection come?" for half of his head had turned white out of fear of the coming of the Hour. He said, "No, I am Jesus son of Mary." So he spoke with him, and he died on the spot. As for the three whom he brought to life, they lived and had children.

﴿And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses.﴾ Jesus would inform a man of what he had eaten in his house the night before, what he eats today, and what he has stored for supper. It was also said that he was in the school, informing the boy of what he had eaten and what his mother had hidden for him of food, so that the boy would go to his mother, weep until she gave him food, and then bring it to Jesus. So they kept the children away from the school. Jesus came in search of them, and they were in a house. He said, "Who are these in the house?" It was said, "Pigs." Jesus said, "Let them be so," and they became pigs by the command of Allah, the Exalted. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 50:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And confirming that which came before me of the Torah⟩. He means: "and I am one who confirms." ﴿And to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you⟩. Abu 'Ubayda said: "By 'some' he intended 'all'; that is, all that was forbidden to you." Similar to this is the saying of the poet:

(Or the souls' doves are bound up ...)

That is, all the souls. It was also said that it is to be taken literally: he had made lawful for them some of what had been forbidden to them in the Torah, namely the flesh of camels and their fat.

﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord⟩. He means: with signs, as we have explained. {So fear Allah and obey me}.
﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ That is: a clear road.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 52:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When Jesus perceived disbelief from them﴾, meaning: he saw it and found disbelief among them. He said: ﴿Who will be my helpers toward God?﴾ It was said that its meaning is: "Who will be my helpers along with God?" But the grammarians (al-nuhat) said: "ilā" (toward) remains in its place and is not in the sense of "maʿa" (with). Rather its meaning is: who will join his help to the help of God for me? ﴿The disciples (al-hawariyyun) said: We are the helpers of God.﴾ Ibn Abi Najih said: The hawariyyun were a people who were launderers (qassarin), and they were named so because they used to bleach clothes.

It was also said: they were fishermen who hunted fish. The correct view is that the hawari is the choice and essence of everything, and from this is his saying about al-Zubayr: "He is the son of my paternal aunt and my hawari from among my community," meaning: my choice and my essence.

The original meaning of hawari is whiteness and cleanliness, so they were named hawariyyun for the purity of their hearts. From this, the women of the cities are called hawariyat. The poet said:

(So say to the hawariyat, weeping for others than us... and let only the barking dogs weep for us)

From this also comes "khubz hawari" (refined bread), because of its purity and whiteness.

As for his saying: ﴿We are the helpers of God﴾, it is because when they helped Jesus, it was as if they had helped God. ﴿We believe in God, and bear witness that we are Muslims.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 53:

God Most High says: ﴿Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down, and we have followed the Messenger, so write us down among the witnesses.﴾ It has been said: "among the witnesses" refers to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), because they bear witness for the messengers that they delivered the message. And it has also been said: among those who bear witness to the prophethood of ʿIsa (Jesus).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed﴾. Makr (scheming) on the part of the servant is deceit (khubth) and trickery (khida'), while makr on the part of Allah, exalted is that He seizes the servant suddenly from where he does not know. He called it makr, by way of correspondence (al-muqabalah), because it is the recompense for their scheming, as He said: ﴿And the recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it﴾. What is meant by their scheming here is that they plotted to kill ʿIsa. A man said: "Shall I not guide you to the house in which ʿIsa is?" So they came with him to the house in which ʿIsa was. Allah raised ʿIsa up to the heaven and cast the likeness of ʿIsa upon the one who had guided them to him, so they seized him while he was crying out, "I am not ʿIsa!" and they killed him. It is also said that the one who guided them was one of the disciples (al-Hawariyyun). That is the scheming of Allah. ﴿And Allah is the best of the schemers﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 55:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When God said: "O Jesus, I am going to cause you to die and will raise you up to Me"﴾. That is: and mention the saying of God to Jesus: "I will cause you to die and will raise you up to Me, and will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me will be your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ." If someone says: What is the meaning of tawaffi (causing to die, taking in full), when Jesus is alive? According to your claim? We say: there are several opinions on this. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: its meaning is: "I am taking you from the earth," and this is correct according to the lexicographers, for it is said: "I took my right in full from so-and-so," meaning: I received it.

Al-Azhari said: It is as if He is saying: "I am causing you to die (i.e., to complete) the number of your forefathers on the earth," and everything that is completed is "mutawaffa" and "mustawfa." Al-Farra' said: In it there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its sense is: "I will raise you up to Me and cause you to die," meaning after descending from the sky.

It has been established from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "The son of Mary will certainly descend as a just ruler who breaks the cross and kills the swine." In another narration: "He will kill the Dajjal at the gate of Lud," which is in Damascus. In the reports it is said that he will live on the earth after that for seven years, and will marry, and will have children. Then he will die, and the believers of this community will pray over him.

This inversion of order that we mentioned in the verse is related from Ibn 'Abbas, and he has another opinion: that the verse is in its literal sense of death, and that Jesus has indeed died, then God revived him and raised him to the sky.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: God caused him to die for three hours of the day, then God revived him and raised him up to Himself. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: tawaffi is sleep, and Jesus had gone to sleep, so God raised him up to the sky while he was asleep. The well-known opinions are the first two.

It has also been narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "I saw my two maternal cousins, Jesus and Yahya, in the second heaven on the night of the Mi'raj." It is also narrated: "that he saw them in the lowest heaven." The first is more sound. He (peace and blessings be upon him) also said: "I saw the Messiah, son of Mary, circumambulating the House." This indicates that the sounder view is that he is alive. In the reports of the Mi'raj: "The Prophet met Adam in the first heaven, Jesus in the second heaven, Joseph in the third heaven, Idris in the fourth heaven, Aaron in the fifth heaven, Moses in the sixth heaven, - and in another narration the seventh heaven - and Abraham in the seventh heaven."

His saying: ﴿and purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: that is, I will release you from their filth and impurities, ﴿and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾.

It was said: He meant by this the Christians, who are above the Jews until the Day of Resurrection, and the Jews are the most humiliated of the two groups; their kingdom has gone and will never return, whereas the kingdom of the Christians endures until near the Hour. It was also said: by those who followed him He meant the community of Muhammad, since they affirmed him and agreed with him in the religion of monotheism, so they are above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection.

Regarding this there are two views: one, that they are above them in argument; and the second, in might and dominance. He (ﷺ) has said: "I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, there being no prophet between me and him."

﴿Then to Me will be your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ﴾.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾. The punishment in this world is killing, captivity, and the jizya (the poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects). The punishment in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿and they will have no helpers
