And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full. [As for the verse:] ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾: meaning, He does not show mercy to the disbelievers, nor does He praise them with good.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That We recite to you of the signs and the Wise Reminder﴾. He means: the Qur'an. "The Wise Reminder" means: the Reminder possessing wisdom (hikmah). It was also said: the Reminder that is firmly established (muhkam), in which corruption cannot find its way.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 59:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus in the sight of God is like the likeness of Adam﴾. The occasion of revelation of this verse is what was narrated: that the delegation of Najran, when they came to the Prophet, he said to them: "Accept Islam." They said: "We are Muslims." He said: "You have lied; three things prevent you from that: your saying that God has taken a son, your prostration to the cross, and your eating of pork." They said: "Who is the father of Jesus?" Then this verse was revealed. In the verse there is evidence against them and a refutation of their saying. So His saying: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus﴾, that is, the attribute of Jesus, ﴿in the sight of God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was﴾. The meaning is: the creation of Jesus without a father is like the creation of Adam without a father or a mother, and the creation of Jesus without a father is no more wondrous than the creation of Adam without a father or a mother.

As for His saying: ﴿Then He said to him, "Be," and he was﴾, it refers to Adam. If someone says: since He mentioned that He created him from dust, what is the meaning of His saying afterwards ﴿Then He said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ after the creation? It is said: its meaning is that He created him from dust, then informed you that I said to him, "Be," and he was, without any order in the creation, as it happens with his descendants. This is like the saying of a man: "I gave you a dirham today, then I gave you a dirham yesterday," i.e., then I inform you that I gave you a dirham yesterday.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 60:

God's words: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾ If it is said: Was he (the Prophet) doubtful about the truth, so that he was forbidden from doubt? It is said: The address is to the Prophet, but what is meant is the community (ummah). It is also said that its meaning is: Say to the one who doubts about it: "The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters."

Know that in what preceded, the illustration (tamthil) of the permissibility of analogy (qiyas) is evidence that qiyas is returning a branch (far') to a root (asl) by some kind of resemblance (shabah). God, exalted is He, returned Jesus to Adam by a certain kind of resemblance, and this indicates the permissibility of qiyas. And the mathal (parable/example) is the mention of a thing that is cited as evidence for something else that shares its meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 61:

The words of God Most High: ﴿Then whoever argues with you concerning it﴾, that is: disputes with you about the truth ﴿after the knowledge has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke earnestly [in mubahala] and lay the curse of God upon the liars"﴾.

This refers to the Prophet's invitation of the people of Najran to mubahala (mutual imprecation).

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas narrated: "The Prophet took the hand of al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Fatimah and Ali, then invited them to mubahala."

So his words ﴿our sons﴾ refer to al-Hasan and al-Husayn; his words ﴿our women﴾ mean Fatimah; and ﴿ourselves﴾ means himself and Ali. If someone asks: how did he say ﴿ourselves﴾ when Ali was other than him? It is said: the Arabs call a man's paternal cousin his "self", and Ali was his paternal cousin. It is also said: he mentioned him generally to include the company of the people of the religion.

Al-ibtihal (invoking earnestly) is al-iltia' (pressing supplication), and from it comes al-bahlah, which is al-la'nah (curse). It is said: "Upon you be the bahlat of God", meaning: the curse of God. Al-ibtihal is striving in supplicating for the curse.

Al-la'nah is removal and expulsion from mercy by way of punishment. Labid said:

(And elders, chiefs of 'Amir, whom time looked upon and so invoked [a curse])

That is: time looked upon them with destruction and so annihilated them through earnest effort against them.

In the narrative: when the Prophet invited them to ibtihal and made the curse fall upon the liar of the two parties, the bishop said to them: "Do not invoke curses, for if you were to invoke against him, the valley would blaze with fire upon you." They said to the Prophet: "Is there anything other than mubahala?" He said: "Islam, or war, or the jizyah." They accepted the jizyah and departed. The Prophet said: "If they had cursed each other, they would have become apes and swine." In another narration: "If they had engaged in mutual cursing, there would not remain on earth a Christian man or a Christian woman until the Day of Resurrection."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾, meaning: the true news. ﴿And there is no deity except Allah﴾. The "min" (مِن) here is a redundant particle (صلة), and its full sense is: "there is no deity except Allah." ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Mighty, the Wise﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 63:

﴿Then if they turn away﴾, i.e., they turn away (aʿrada). ﴿then indeed Allah is All-Knowing of the corrupters﴾, i.e., of those among them who spread corruption.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 64:

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture⦆ The address is to the Jews and the Christians. ﴿Come to a word⦆ The Arabs call every matter that has an explanation a "kalimah" (word), and from this the qasidah (ode) is called a kalimah.

﴿Common⦆ That is, just (ʿadl). From this is the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma:

"Show me a course in which there is no wrong, / in which equality (al-sawa') is established between us."

"If equality is abandoned, then there is no meeting / between you and us, the sons of ʿAmr."

By al-sawa' he meant justice (al-ʿadl).

﴿That we worship none but Allah⦆ The cause of this: the Jews said, "Muhammad wants nothing from us except that we worship him," and the Christians said the same. So the verse was revealed: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word common between us and you⦆. Its meaning: come to a matter upon which we are equal, namely that we worship none but Allah, and that we all agree upon His worship. ﴿And that we associate nothing with Him⦆.

﴿And that some of us do not take others as lords besides Allah⦆. ʿIkrimah said: That is, some of us should not prostrate to others, for whoever prostrates to another has taken him as a lord.

It was also said: it is obedience to created beings in disobedience to the Creator. ﴿But if they turn away⦆, that is, if they turn away, ﴿then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims⦆, that is, by this word and this matter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 65:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿O People of the Book, why do you argue about Abraham?﴾ The occasion of revelation of the verse: the Jews and the Christians disputed before the Prophet concerning Abraham. The Jews said: "He is of us." The Christians said: "No, rather he is of us." So there was revealed His words: ﴿why do you argue﴾, meaning, why do you dispute ﴿about Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Will you not then reason?﴾ Its meaning is that Judaism is a distortion of the Torah, and Christianity is a distortion of the Gospel, and the Torah and the Gospel were sent down after Abraham.

So how can you claim that he was upon Judaism or upon Christianity? As for the Torah (al-Tawrah) and the Gospel (al-Injil), we have already mentioned their derivation, and it has been said that they have no derivation, and that they are two names in Syriac.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 66:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Here you are, you people﴾. "Ha" (hā) is for alerting attention, and its meaning is: O you people, you ﴿argued﴾, that is, disputed ﴿concerning that of which you have knowledge; so why do you argue concerning that of which you have no knowledge﴾? That is: you disputed about the matter of Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus), and you claimed to be upon the religion of Musa and Isa, and indeed the revelation concerning him was sent down to you. So why do you dispute about the matter of Ibrahim (Abraham), when it was not sent down to you, and you have no knowledge of it?! ﴿But Allah knows, and you do not know﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 67:

The words of God the Exalted: ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian﴾. God the Exalted informed that he was not upon what they claimed of Judaism and [nor] Christianity, ﴿but he was a ḥanīf, a Muslim﴾.

Al-ḥanīf (one who inclines toward the religion and stays firm upon it): it is the one who inclines toward the religion and is steadfast upon it. From this comes al-Aḥnaf (the one whose feet lean inward), which is one who leans in his step. Mujāhid said: al-ḥanīf is the one who follows. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-ḥanīf is the one who performs the ḥajj.

If someone says: why did He say ﴿a ḥanīf, a Muslim﴾, when the Muslim is the one who holds to everything that Muhammad, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), brought, and Abraham was not upon the whole of his sharia?

It is said: he was upon part of his sharia, and so he was a Muslim by that. Like someone from this community who died at the beginning of the matter, he was a Muslim by part of its sharia, for it was only completed and established at the end of the matter. It is also possible that His words ﴿Muslim﴾ mean submission, from His words: ﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds"﴾. Therefore He said: ﴿a ḥanīf, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him﴾: those who followed him in his time. ﴿And this Prophet﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and those who believe﴾, meaning: from this community. ﴿And Allah is the Ally of the believers﴾.

Almost all of this is the commentator's gloss on Q. 3:69, so the translation follows it closely.

The Exalted said: ﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could mislead you﴾. That is, a group of the People of the Book wished. ﴿They could mislead you﴾: they could turn you back to misguidance, and to what they themselves hold of Judaism and Christianity. ﴿Yet they mislead none but themselves, and they do not perceive﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 70:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while you bear witness?﴾ In this there are two opinions. The first: its meaning is: Why do you disbelieve in the description and attributes of Muhammad (ﷺ) while you witness them in the Torah and the Gospel?

And the second: its meaning is: Why do you disbelieve in what Muhammad brings of proofs and miracles, while you acknowledge the like of them that were brought by Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus)?

"Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?﴾ Its meaning: Why do you mix belief in Jesus, who is the truth, with disbelief in Muhammad, who is falsehood? It has also been said that its meaning is: Why do you cover the truth concerning the description of Muhammad with alteration, which is falsehood?"

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 72:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And a group of the People of the Book said: "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they may return."﴾ As for "wajh al-nahar" (the face of the day): it is its beginning. From this is the saying of the poet:

(Whoever is delighted by the killing of Malik, / let him come to our women at the face of the day.)

That is, at the beginning of the day. This refers to the Jews. They said: "We will believe in Muhammad at the beginning of the day, and then disbelieve in him at the end of the day, so that people will suspect him (yatahamuhu) and say: 'Something has appeared from him,' until they disbelieve in him." It was also said that they said: "We will affirm him in part and deny him in part, so that people will say: 'They affirmed him where he was truthful, and denied him where he was untruthful,' and so they will doubt his state (fayastaribun bi-halihi)."

﴿That perhaps they may return﴾: that is, those who follow him in his religion. And "wajh al-nahar" and "akhiruhu" will mean "some" according to the second opinion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not believe except for one who follows your religion﴾, meaning: do not believe (affirm the truth of) anyone except one who follows your religion. The "lam" in it (in li-man) is extra (ziyadah), as in His saying: ﴿Perhaps some of what you seek to hasten has drawn near to you﴾, meaning: has drawn near to you (radifakum, "followed you"). This is also said of the Jews: they said, "Do not believe except one who agrees with you in your religion."

Then God, may He be exalted, began and said: ﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God﴾, meaning: indeed, clarification (al-bayan) is the clarification of God.

﴿That anyone be given the like of what you have been given﴾, meaning: and that they not argue against you before your Lord; for the proof is yours against them, and not theirs against you before God.

Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mubarrad said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse. His saying ﴿And do not believe﴾ means: do not affirm the truth of ﴿that anyone be given the like of what you have been given﴾, i.e., of the proofs (dalalat) and signs (ayat), such as the manna and the quails (al-manna wa al-salwa) and the like.

﴿Except for one who follows your religion﴾ means: except for one who agrees with you in Judaism. ﴿Or that they argue against you before your Lord﴾ means: if you affirm their truth, they will argue against you on the Day of Resurrection before your Lord, saying, "We are like you, or better than you," so do not believe them, lest they argue against you before your Lord. Up to this point is the speech of the Jews. Then God, may He be exalted, began and said: ﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God.﴾ It was also said that its meaning is: ﴿And do not believe except for one who follows your religion﴾, meaning: and do not affirm that prophethood is among other than the children of Isaac, and that it is among the children of Ishmael.

[His saying, may He be exalted] {Say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.

(He singles out for His mercy whom He wills.) Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the religion (al-dīn). Mujahid said: it is prophethood (al-nubuwwah). Ibn Jurayj said: it is the Qur'an and Islam. (﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 75:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾. We have already mentioned the opinions regarding the qintar (a large measure of wealth). ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said: it is six thousand dinars.

This was concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām: a man deposited with him two thousand and two hundred ounces of gold, and he discharged the trust in it.

﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾. This was concerning Finḥāṣ ibn ʿĀzūrāʾ the Jew: a man deposited a dinar with him and he betrayed it.

﴿Except as long as you stand over him﴾, i.e., he will not return it to you unless you are standing over his head, demanding it. It was said: by "standing" he meant insistence and demanding.

﴿That is because they say: "There is no blame upon us regarding the common people."﴾ The Jews said: there is no sin upon us in taking the wealth of the Arabs, as if they considered the wealth of the common people lawful, namely the Arabs, Muhammad and his companions.

﴿And they speak falsehood against God while they know﴾

Surah 3, verse 76 in al-Sam'ani's commentary:

﴿Balā﴾ (Yes, indeed): ʿalayhim sabīl (there is a way against them); he mentioned it as a response to their claim.

The grammarians (al-nuḥāh) said: this is a complete pause (waqf tāmm), and then he begins, saying: ﴿Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of God﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "and is mindful of God" means he avoids shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿for God loves the mindful (al-muttaqīn)﴾, meaning the monotheists (al-muwaḥḥidūn).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 77:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾. Abu Wa'il, who is Shaqiq ibn Salama, related from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever swears a false oath in order to seize by it the property of a Muslim man will meet Allah while He is angry with him." Then he recited this verse. He said: Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays was present, and he said: "It was revealed concerning me," and he mentioned an account. This is a hadith in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Muslim related it in his Sahih by another narration, and he added that: "It was said: O Messenger of Allah, even if it concerns something small? He said: Even if it concerns a twig of arak (a tree)."

Muslim also related in his book, by a third narration, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Three people, Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: the one who reminds people of his giving, the one who lets his garment hang below the ankles, and the one who sells his merchandise with a false oath."

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾, meaning: a small amount of the worldly goods. ﴿Those will have no share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: they will have no portion in it.

﴿And Allah will not speak to them﴾, meaning: He will not speak to them as He speaks to the believers. It is established that He, may His majesty be glorified, speaks to the believers on the Day of Resurrection without an interpreter. It was also said that it means anger, as one says: "I do not speak to so-and-so," when one is angry with him. ﴿Nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: He will not look at them with mercy.

﴿Nor will He purify them﴾, meaning: He will not praise them with good, nor will He cleanse them of sins. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 78:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, among them is a group who distort the Book with their tongues﴾, meaning: they alter and distort the Book with their tongues. It is also said: they turn their tongues away from the Book. ﴿So that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book. And they say, "It is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak falsehood about Allah while they know﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and prophethood﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: that the Jews and the Christians gathered before the Prophet (ﷺ) and disputed concerning Abraham. Each group said, "He is one of us." He said, "You have lied." They became angry and said, "O Muhammad, you want nothing from us except that we take you as a lord." So the verse was revealed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 79:

﴿It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Book﴾ meaning: the Qur'an; ﴿and the judgment﴾ meaning: the rulings; and the wisdom (ḥikmah): the Sunnah; ﴿and prophethood﴾ meaning: the lofty station of the prophets.

﴿Then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than to Allah"﴾, meaning: be slaves to me rather than to Allah. It was also said that by "human" he meant ʿĪsā, may Allah's blessings be upon him, because they claimed that ʿĪsā had commanded them to worship him and take him as a lord. So He said: ﴿It is not for a human﴾, meaning ʿĪsā,

﴿that Allah should give him the Book﴾, meaning: the Gospel (Injīl), ﴿and the judgment and prophethood. Then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than to Allah." But rather, "Be rabbānīyīn (people devoted to the Lord) by what you have been teaching of the Book"﴾.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: the rabbānī is the learned jurist who acts upon his knowledge. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the rabbānī is the knowledgeable, wise scholar. And in a report: "Be scholars, forbearing ones."

In terms of meaning, the rabbānī is one who is upon the religion of the Lord and upon the path of the Lord.

It was also said that the word derives from tarbiyah (upbringing): the rabbānī is one who was raised up on the minor parts of knowledge until he reached its major parts. It is reported that when Ibn ʿAbbās died, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah stood over his grave and said: "Today the rabbānī of this community has died."

Mujāhid said: the rabbāniyyūn are above the aḥbār (rabbis); the aḥbār are the scholars, and the rabbāniyyūn are those who combined knowledge with insight into managing people.

﴿by what you have been teaching﴾ — with the shaddah (tuʿallimūn, from teaching) — of the Qur'an; and with the lighter form, from knowledge (ʿilm).

﴿and by what you have been studying (tadrusūn)﴾, meaning: reciting.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 80:

His Exalted saying: ﴿Nor would He order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords﴾. It is read with a raised ra' (wa-la yamurukum, nominative), on the basis of a new sentence (ibtida'), meaning: "Nor would Allah order you..." It is also read with a fathah on the ra' (wa-la yamurakum), in coordination (nasaq), meaning: "Nor would that human being order you..." ﴿to take the angels and the prophets as lords﴾. So the Christians are those who took the prophets as lords, and the Sabians are those who took the angels as lords.

﴿Would He order you to disbelieve after you have submitted [to Allah]?﴾ That is: He would not order you to disbelieve after Islam.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 81:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book." ﴿Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom﴾: this is one of the two views concerning the meaning of the well-known recitation. Ibn 'Abbas said: the meaning of the verse is: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book, together with the prophets." Ibn 'Abbas said: When God brought forth the offspring from the loins of Adam like specks, the prophets among them were like lamps and lanterns, and He took the covenant from the prophets that they would believe in Muhammad, affirm him, and support him if they lived to see him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets: whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom﴾. Hamza recited "lamma ataytukum" with a light pronunciation and a kasra on the lam, and others recited "lamma ataytukum" with a fatha on the lam and a shadda. The well-known recitation is with a fatha on the lam and no shadda, and its meaning is: "that which I have given you," in the sense of a statement.

It has also been said: its meaning is "if I give you," in the sense of a conditional: ﴿Then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him and surely support him﴾, meaning Muhammad.

﴿He said: Do you acknowledge?﴾ That is, acknowledge. ﴿And take upon that My burden?﴾ That is, My covenant. The iṣr is the heavy covenant. ﴿They said: We acknowledge. He said: Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.﴾

Al-Dahhak said: the covenant was taken only from the prophets, as the verse expresses, so a covenant was taken from every prophet that he would believe in the prophet who would come after him and support him. Thus a covenant was taken from Moses, peace be upon him, that he would believe in Jesus, and from Jesus that he would believe in Muhammad, and similar to that.

Then He said: ﴿So whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun).﴾ ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of God?﴾ "Yabghun" means "yatlubun" (they seek). It is read with the "ya" and with the "ta."

﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: When He addressed them with His words, ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾, all of them submitted, and they said, "Yes." But some of them said "yes" willingly, and some of them unwillingly. It was also said: Whoever is in the heavens submitted willingly, and whoever is on the earth submitted both willingly and unwillingly, some of them willingly and some of them unwillingly, out of fear of the sword. ﴿And to Him you will be returned.﴾

Then He said: ﴿So whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun).﴾ ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of God?﴾ "Yabghun" means "yatlubun" (they seek). It is read with the "ya" and with the "ta."

﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: When He addressed them with His words, ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾, all of them submitted, and they said, "Yes." But some of them said "yes" willingly, and some of them unwillingly. It was also said: Whoever is in the heavens submitted willingly, and whoever is on the earth submitted both willingly and unwillingly, some of them willingly and some of them unwillingly, out of fear of the sword. ﴿And to Him you will be returned.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 84:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: We believe in God, and in what has been sent down to us, and in what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and in what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are submitting.﴾ When He mentioned the kingdom and the religions, and the people's confusion concerning them, He commanded His Messenger to say: ﴿We believe in God﴾, and so on to the end of the verse. We have already mentioned the meaning of "the Tribes" (al-asbat) and what has been said about it. ﴿And what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord...﴾

Almost; I'll translate it now.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter﴾. And it is fitting for whoever seeks a religion other than the religion of Islam that he should become, tomorrow, among the losers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and who testified that the Messenger is true and clear proofs had come to them?﴾ He means: Allah will not guide them. This is like the saying of Abdullah ibn Qays al-Ruqayyat:

(How can I sleep on the bed, when the cares have swept over me in a fierce raid?)

That is, I have no sleep on the bed.

The verse was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn AwS ibn al-Samit, for he apostatized from Islam and joined Makkah, and he remained there for a period. Then he sent to the Muslims asking that he be allowed to return to Islam, and the verse was revealed: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief?﴾

Al-Zajjaj said: He means that they deserve misguidance and do not deserve guidance. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 87:

﴿Those—their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together.﴾

If someone says: Why did He say ﴿and of mankind, all together﴾? Does that not also include Himself? So how would He curse Himself? It is said: He meant that on the Day of Resurrection some of them will curse one another, and they will curse themselves. It is also said: They will curse the wrongdoers and the disbelievers, and that is their cursing of themselves, because whoever curses the wrongdoers and the disbelievers, while he himself is a wrongdoer and a disbeliever, has cursed himself.

﴿Abiding therein; their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be reprieved, except for those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ He means by this al-Harith ibn Aws, for he repented, embraced Islam, and his repentance was accepted.

﴿Abiding therein; their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be reprieved, except for those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ He means by this al-Harith ibn Aws, for he repented, embraced Islam, and his repentance was accepted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 90:

The Most High's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve after their belief and then increase in disbelief, their repentance will never be accepted﴾. This was revealed concerning a people who were with al-Harith ibn Aws and apostatized. When he returned to Islam, those people held back from Islam, and they said: "We will await the turns of fate for Muhammad. If time favours him and his command prevails, we will return to his religion." So the verse was revealed.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve after their belief﴾ means: they apostatized from Islam after their belief. ﴿Then increase in disbelief﴾ by their saying: "We await for Muhammad the vicissitudes of fate." ﴿Their repentance will never be accepted﴾. Abu al-'Aliyah said: because they were not sincere in repentance, but were waiting (to see what would happen). ﴿And those are the wrongdoers﴾. It was also said: He meant by this: those who disbelieved after their belief in Jesus, and then increased in disbelief in Muhammad. ﴿Their repentance will never be accepted﴾ among people. ﴿And those are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 91:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold, even if he should offer it in ransom.﴾ That is, even if he offers it in ransom. The "wa" (and) here is extra (zā'idah) and inserted (muqḥamah). It has also been said: the sense of the verse is: never will be accepted from any of them that he donate the filling of the earth with gold, and even if he offers it in ransom likewise, it will not be accepted. ﴿Those — for them is a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 92:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, Amr ibn Maymun and Masruq ibn al-Ajda' Abu 'Aisha said: "Al-birr (righteousness) here means Paradise." It was also said that it means righteous deeds, and it was said that it means reward. In a report: "Hold to truthfulness, for it guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to Paradise. Beware of lying, for lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the Fire."

﴿Until you spend from what you love﴾. It was said: by spending is meant paying zakat. It was said: paying all kinds of charity. It was said: every spending by which one seeks the pleasure of Allah the Exalted, through which one attains this righteousness.

It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, Abu Talha said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see that Allah asks us for our wealth. I call you to witness that I have given such-and-such orchard to Allah the Exalted." He said: "Give it in charity to the poor, to your relatives." So he gave it to his kin, among them Ubayy and Hassan.

It is narrated that Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, bought a slave-girl whom he had desired. When he looked at her, he freed her, married her to a man, and recited the words of Allah the Exalted: (﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love. And whatever you spend, indeed Allah knows it﴾), meaning: He knows it, i.e., He will reward it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 93:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾. The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of the verse: the Jews said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "You claim that you are upon the religion (milla) of Ibrahim (Abraham), and he did not eat camel meat and its milk, while you eat them. So you are not upon the religion of Ibrahim." So the verse was revealed: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was sent down﴾. That is: the matter is not as they said, that the prohibition of camel meat and its milk was upon Ibrahim. Rather, "all" (al-kull) was lawful to him and to the Children of Israel. Israel (Ya'qub) made them unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. That is: their prohibition is not in the Torah, nor in the law (shar') of Ibrahim; it is only something that Israel made unlawful for himself. The reason for his making that unlawful for himself was that he suffered from sciatica (irq al-nasa), and he had from it a cry (zaqa'), meaning a shout. So he said: "If God cures me of it, I will surely make unlawful the food most beloved to me, camel meat and its milk." God cured him, so he made them unlawful for himself.

﴿Say: Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾. He challenged them to bring the Torah as proof of what they claimed, but they did not bring it, since its prohibition was not in the Torah. Thus they were unable to bring the Torah, and that was like a miracle (mu'jiza) for the Messenger over them.

"The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then whoever fabricates lies against Allah after that, they are the wrongdoers﴾. We have already mentioned the meaning of iftira' (fabrication) and of zulm (wrongdoing)."

"His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Allah has spoken the truth﴾, meaning: in what He has informed and revealed. ﴿So follow the religion of Abraham, a true monotheist (ḥanīf)﴾. He only called them to follow the religion of Abraham because in following his religion is following him, and in following him is following his religion. ﴿And he was not of the polytheists﴾."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 96:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾. Abu Dharr narrated that he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which mosque was established first?" He said: "The Sacred Mosque." (I said:) "Then which?" He said: "The Farthest Mosque (al-Masjid al-Aqsa)." I said: "How long was between them?" He said: "Forty years." Then he said: "Wherever prayer overtakes you, pray, for it is a mosque for you."

Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah narrated from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: He meant by it that the first House established for mankind, blessed, with mercy and blessing, and the clear signs are in the one at Bakkah.

It was said: The first thing Allah Most High created from the earth was the site of the House, and then from it the whole earth was created. ﴿Whoever enters it is safe. And for Allah, upon mankind, is a pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find a way to it. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need﴾.

The first of the mountains created was Mount Abu Qubays.

In the stories (al-Qasas) it is related that Allah Most High commanded the angels to build the House two thousand years before the creation of Adam, and the angels used to perform pilgrimage to it. When Adam performed the pilgrimage, the angels said: "May your pilgrimage be accepted; we performed pilgrimage to this House two thousand years before you."

As for Bakkah, the correct view is that Bakkah and Makkah have one meaning, and this is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas. Similar to it: ṭīnun lāzib and lāzim (sticky clay), and samala ra'sahu and sabala (he shaved his head), with one meaning.

It was said: Bakkah is the site of the House, and Makkah is the whole town. It was also said: it was named Bakkah because people crowd (yatabakkawna) there, that is, they throng together. From this is the saying of the poet:

(When the drinker is seized by drunkenness... then leave him until he is crowded (yabukk) in a crowd)

And His saying: ﴿blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾, meaning: that House was established as a place of blessing and a guidance for the worlds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 97:

﴿In it are clear signs: the standing place of Abraham﴾ It was recited: "In it is a clear sign (āyah bayyinah)," in the singular, namely the standing place of Abraham. The well-known reading is: ﴿In it are clear signs: the standing place of Abraham﴾.

Among those signs: the standing place of Abraham, which is the stone on which there is a mark of the toes of Abraham's foot. Its trace remained upon it, but it wore away from the great number of hands that touched it. It was also said that the standing place of Abraham is the entire Sacred Precinct (al-Haram).

Among the signs in the House also: birds fly but do not fly over it, so it is said. Among them: when a hunting bird pursues game and the game enters the Sacred Precinct, the bird refrains from it. Among them: no tyrant has ever targeted it except that God, exalted is He, broke him. Among them: when rain falls on the Yemeni Corner (al-Rukn al-Yamani), there is fertility in Yemen; and if it falls on the Syrian side, there is fertility in Syria; and if it falls on all sides, there is fertility on all sides.

The cause of this is that the Jews said: "Our qiblah is more worthy than your qiblah." So God, exalted is He, made clear to the Muslims the honour of their qiblah, for it was singled out with things that were not given to their qiblah, and that Bayt al-Maqdis was burned and destroyed, whereas the Ka'bah: no tyrant has targeted it except that God, exalted is He, broke him. ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the one who has committed a crime enters it, and becomes safe from being killed within it, but he is not to be fed or given drink, nor to be sold or to buy, until he leaves and is then killed.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and the majority of the exegetes—and this is the most correct view—said: he intended safety from the Unbelievers snatching people away by killing and raiding. It was also said: he intended by it: whoever enters it will be safe on the Day of Resurrection from the punishment.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House﴾. We have already mentioned the meaning of hajj.

﴿For whoever is able to make his way thereto﴾. Al-Hasan related in a mursal report from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he was asked about capability (al-istita'ah), and he said: "Provision and mount." Ibn 'Umar related that he was asked: "Which pilgrims are best?" He said: "The dishevelled, the unperfumed." It was asked: "Which pilgrimage is best?" He said: "The one with raising the voice (in talbiyah) and the sacrifice of blood." It was asked: "What is the sabil (way)?" He said: "Provision and mount."

Malik said: capability is by bodily strength; whenever one finds provision and is strong enough to walk, the pilgrimage becomes obligatory for him. The most correct view is that capability is the power to reach what conveys one to the pilgrimage; among it is provision and mount, and among it is safety of the road, and maintenance of one's family, and the like.

﴿And whoever disbelieves, then God is Self-Sufficient above the worlds﴾. The most correct view is that by disbelief he meant denying the obligation of the pilgrimage. It was also said: when the verse ﴿And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered people of all religions and said: "God has prescribed for you the pilgrimage, O people, so make the pilgrimage." The believers affirmed him, and the disbelievers denied him; so there was revealed: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then God is Self-Sufficient above the worlds﴾.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Say: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah, while Allah is witness over what you do?﴾ That is: nothing of what you do is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 99:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O People of the Book, why do you bar from the way of God those who believe?﴾ That is: (why do you prevent those who believe from the way of God) by concealing the description of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Seeking to make it crooked﴾ That is: you seek deviation from the way and turning away from it by altering the description of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿While you are witnesses﴾ meaning: you know that it is true, according to what its description and attributes were transmitted. ﴿And God is not unaware of what you do﴾.

O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you to disbelief after your belief.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you to disbelief after your belief.﴾ Meaning: they will return you to Judaism and Christianity.

How can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you? Al-Akhfash Sa'id ibn Mas'ada said: "In what state would you disbelieve?!"

If someone says: his prohibiting them from disbelief by the Messenger being among them implies the permissibility of disbelief in a state where the Messenger is not among them. It is said: there is no state in which the Messenger is not among them, for although he is today outside their midst, his law (shar') remains among them, so it is as though he were among them.

And whoever holds fast to Allah (ya'tasim billah), then he has been guided to a straight path. That is: whoever seeks protection in Allah (yamtani' billah). It is said: whoever trusts in Allah (yathiq billah) has been guided to a straight path.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 102:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: It means that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not denied. Qatadah said: The verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by His statement: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: Abrogation does not hold in this case, and His statement ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ is an explanation of this verse, because whoever obeys Allah at the time when obedience is obligatory, remembers Him at the time when remembrance is obligatory, and thanks Him in the place where thanks is obligatory, has indeed feared Allah as He should be feared.

This has not become abrogated, and His statement ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ agrees with it, because taqwa, if it is in the place of command and obligation, and commands and obligations are according to capacity, then one of the two verses agrees with the other, so abrogation does not hold in it.

﴿And do not die except while you are Muslims﴾. If someone says: How did He forbid them from dying in disbelief, when death does not fall under command and prohibition? It is said: Its meaning is: remain upon Islam, so that when death reaches you, it finds you upon Islam. This is like a man saying to another: "Let me not see you doing such-and-such" (la aritak taf'al kadha). Its meaning is: do not do such-and-such, so that when I see you (la) I do not see you doing it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 103:

The Exalted said: ﴿And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The rope of Allah is the covenant." Qatada (and al-Suddi) said: "The rope of Allah is the Qur'an." It is also reported in a khabar: "The Qur'an is a rope stretched out (one end) in the hand of Allah and (the other end) in your hands." It was also said: "The ḥabl (rope) is the path (ṭarīq), the rope of Allah is the path of Allah." They cited, in describing the she-camel, the verse of the poet:

"And when she passes the ropes (paths) of one tribe, / Its ropes (paths) descend to you from the other."

That is, its path. The original meaning of ḥabl (rope) is anything that connects you to a thing so that you attain it. The covenant is a ḥabl, the Qur'an is a ḥabl, and from this comes the well-known ḥabl (rope), because it leads to the goal.

﴿And do not be divided﴾. The reason for the revelation of the verse is what is related: that two men, one from the Aws and the other from the Khazraj, quarrelled, and each of them called his tribe. The two clans rose up, drew their swords, and it nearly came to fighting between them. This reached the Messenger of Allah, who went out to them riding a donkey and stood between them. Then the verse was revealed, and he recited it to them, and they wept, and each one walked to his companion, embraced him, reconciled, and refrained from fighting. Jabir said: "There was no day worse at its beginning than that day, nor better at its end than that day."

So His saying ﴿And do not be divided﴾ is addressed to them. ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾, meaning: by Islam, the sending of the Messenger, and the sending down of the Book.

﴿When you were enemies﴾, because there had been fighting between the Aws and the Khazraj for a hundred and twenty years. ﴿And He brought your hearts together﴾, meaning: through Islam. ﴿So you became, by His favour, brothers﴾ (i.e., in religion).

﴿And you were on the brink of a pit﴾, i.e., the edge of a pit ﴿of the Fire, and He saved you from it﴾.

It was also said: the verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of the Arabs, but the first [view is more sound], and it is the saying of ʿIkrima. ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, that you may be guided﴾, i.e., that you may be rightly guided and take the path of truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 104:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Let there be among you a community﴾, meaning: be a community. The word "min" (from, among) here is for genus (jins), not for partitive (tab'id). It is like His saying: ﴿So shun the abomination of the idols﴾, and what is meant is shunning the genus of idols entirely, not some of the idols. Likewise His saying: ﴿Let there be among you a community﴾, meaning: be a community ﴿who call to good, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And those are the successful ones﴾, meaning: and you are the successful ones.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verses 105–106:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who became divided and differed﴾, meaning: the Jews and the Christians.

﴿after the clear proofs had come to them. And those – for them is a great punishment﴾, meaning: and those, for them is a great punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Then He described that day, saying: ﴿On the Day when faces will turn white and faces will turn black﴾, meaning: [faces turn white] with monotheism [tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness)] and [faces turn black] with polytheism (shirk). It was also said: faces turn white with the Sunnah and faces turn black with innovation (bid'ah). It was also said that He intended by this: in this world, faces turn white with contentment and faces turn black with greed. The first is more sound, and His saying, may He be exalted, supports it: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, joyful﴾, and so on.

In the narration of Abu Umamah from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The faces of the Kharijites will turn black." ﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?"﴾, i.e., it will be said to them: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?!" If someone asks: how could they disbelieve after belief when they had never been believers at all? It is said that He intended by it the belief of the Day of the Covenant, and that they disbelieved after it.

It was also said: He intended by it the Jews, who believed in what was in the Torah concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), then disbelieved and altered [it]. ﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verses 105–106:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who became divided and differed﴾, meaning: the Jews and the Christians.

﴿after the clear proofs had come to them. And those – for them is a great punishment﴾, meaning: and those, for them is a great punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Then He described that day, saying: ﴿On the Day when faces will turn white and faces will turn black﴾, meaning: [faces turn white] with monotheism [tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness)] and [faces turn black] with polytheism (shirk). It was also said: faces turn white with the Sunnah and faces turn black with innovation (bid'ah). It was also said that He intended by this: in this world, faces turn white with contentment and faces turn black with greed. The first is more sound, and His saying, may He be exalted, supports it: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, joyful﴾, and so on.

In the narration of Abu Umamah from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The faces of the Kharijites will turn black." ﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?"﴾, i.e., it will be said to them: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?!" If someone asks: how could they disbelieve after belief when they had never been believers at all? It is said that He intended by it the belief of the Day of the Covenant, and that they disbelieved after it.

It was also said: He intended by it the Jews, who believed in what was in the Torah concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), then disbelieved and altered [it]. ﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 107:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As for those whose faces turn white, they shall be in the mercy of Allah﴾, that is, in the reward of Allah, ﴿they will abide therein forever﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verses 108–109:

﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth. And Allah does not desire injustice for the worlds.﴾ Because He punishes whoever He punishes for a deserved reason, with justice. ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verses 108–109:

﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth. And Allah does not desire injustice for the worlds.﴾ Because He punishes whoever He punishes for a deserved reason, with justice. ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 110:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾. If someone asks: what is the meaning of His saying, ﴿You are the best nation﴾, and when were they in that state? It is said: He meant by it, "You were the best nation in the Preserved Tablet" (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). And it is said: He meant by it, "You became the best nation when you believed." And it is said: On the Day of Resurrection it will be said to them: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong﴾. So al-ma'ruf (the right) is what the Sharia has recognized, and al-munkar (the wrong) is what the Sharia has disapproved. And in a hadith: "You will certainly enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or else Allah will soon send His punishment upon you all." And he (ﷺ) said: "The best of martyrs after the martyrs of Uhud is a man who stood before an oppressive ruler, enjoined him to do what is right and forbade him from what is wrong, and so he was killed for it."

His saying: ﴿And you believe in Allah. Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them﴾. There is no doubt about this. ﴿Among them are the believers, but most of them are defiant wrongdoers﴾, because some of them believed and most of them disbelieved.

﴿They will not harm you except with a little injury﴾. That is, they will not harm you beyond a minor injury, and this is slight harm; the injury is what is inflicted by the tongue.

﴿And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you; then they will not be victorious﴾. That is: they will be defeated, and victory will be yours over them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 112:

His the Exalted's saying: ﴿Humiliation has been decreed upon them﴾, meaning: the humiliation of disbelief, by killing, captivity, and seizure as spoils of war. ﴿Wherever they are found﴾, meaning: wherever they are found.

﴿Except by a rope from Allah﴾, meaning: the covenant of dhimma (protected status under Muslim rule). ﴿And a rope from the people﴾, which is the covenant of safe-conduct (aman), meaning: they are to be killed and taken captive, except if they have a dhimma or an aman.

﴿And they have earned anger from Allah﴾, meaning: they returned bearing the anger of Allah. (And it was said: the anger of Allah has become binding upon them.) It is from their saying "tabawwa'a makanaka kadha," meaning: he settled in such-and-such a place, i.e., he became bound to it. ﴿And humiliation and poverty have been decreed upon them﴾, meaning: the humiliation of disbelief, displayed in the guise of poverty. This applied to the Jews, so that no Jew would be seen except in the appearance of poverty, even if he was wealthy. ﴿That is because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.﴾

ﷻ"They are not all alike." That is: (the believers and the disbelievers) are not alike. This is a complete pause (waqf tamm), and then a new start: ﴿Among the People of the Book is a community standing (upright)﴾, meaning: just (ʿādila). It was also said: "standing" means upright and steadfast upon the truth. It was also said: the ummah is the path, the straight way, which is the way of truth. Its implied meaning is: "Among the People of the Book there is one possessing an upright community (dhū ummah qāʾima)." From this is the saying of al-Nābigha:

(You burdened me with the sin of a man and abandoned him, / Yet would one who possesses an ummah (dhū ummah) sin while being obedient?) That is: one possessing religion and a way (dhū dīn wa-ṭarīqa).

﴿They recite the verses of God during the hours of the night﴾: the periods of the night. Its singular is inā and anā.

﴿And they prostrate themselves﴾. Ibn Masʿūd said: that is, they pray the ʿatama prayer (ʿishāʾ). It was also said that it refers to prayer between maghrib and ʿishāʾ, and that is during the hours of the night.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 114:

﴿They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they hasten to do good deeds. And those are among the righteous.﴾ He, exalted is He, described them and gave them thanks.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 115:

﴿And whatever good they do, it will never be denied them.﴾ That is, they will be rewarded for it. When Allah rewards a servant for his deed, He has thanked him. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the God-fearing.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 116:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all﴾. That is: their wealth will not repel (punishment) by way of ransom, nor their children by way of support, from the punishment of Allah. This is because a person defends himself with the ransom of wealth, and sometimes by seeking the help of his children. ﴿And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 3, verse 117:

(His saying): ﴿The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind in which is a cold chill﴾. The word ṣirr (ṣirr) in relation to wind means cold. The poet said:

(Kindle, for the night is a night of cold, and the wind, O kindler, is a wind of chill.)

(Perhaps we shall see a fire for the passer-by; if you bring in a guest, then you are free.)

﴿It strikes the tilth of a people who have wronged themselves and destroys it﴾. He likened their spending to a crop struck by a calamity, or that a cold wind struck and destroyed it.

They differed concerning that expenditure. Some said: it refers to the spending of Abu Sufyan on the Day of Badr and Uhud on the polytheists in fighting the Muslims. It was said that it refers to the spending of a person who spends his wealth out of showing off and for reputation, not seeking the Face of Allah. ﴿And Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimate companions (bitanah) those other than your own (people)﴾ — that is, close confidants from outside your religious community. The bitanah (inner circle) of a man is his close associates, those who are privy to his affairs; and from this comes bitanah in a garment, because it lies against the body's inner part (al-baṭn) and the inside (al-bāṭin). This is in the prohibition against allying with the disbelievers. ﴿They spare no effort to corrupt you (la yaʾlūnakum khabālan)﴾ — that is, they fall short regarding your affairs, so they corrupt your affairs for you. Khabāl means corruption. ﴿They love what distresses you (wadda mā ʿanittum)﴾ — that is, they love what is hard for you. ʿUnt means hardship, and from it comes the phrase "al-akmah al-ʿanūt," which is the one that is difficult to climb. Al-Suddi said: he meant by this that they love to return you to disbelief and misguidance.

﴿Hatred has already appeared from their mouths﴾ — meaning, slander with the tongue. ﴿And what their chests conceal is greater﴾ — (meaning: what is in their chests) of rage is greater than slander with the tongue. ﴿We have already made the signs clear to you, if you use your reason.﴾"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 119:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Here you are, you who love them﴾, meaning: you, O people, ﴿love them﴾, that is, you love their faith. ﴿But they do not love you, while you believe in the whole Book﴾, and ﴿when they meet you they say, "We believe,"﴾ meaning: with the tongue.

﴿And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. Say: "Die in your rage." Indeed, Allah is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾. This is an expression for intense rage.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them; but if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. And if you are patient and mindful of Allah, their scheming will not harm you at all.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah encompasses what they do.﴾

Abu (Ubayy ibn Ka'b) said: [the good] is fertility and victory; [it distresses them]. ﴿But if an evil befalls you﴾ means: drought and affliction.

﴿If you are patient and mindful of Allah﴾ means: in hardship and affliction.

﴿Their scheming will not harm you at all﴾. It is also recited as "لا يضركم" (lā yaḍurrakum) with a kasra on the ḍād and with a single rāʾ (lā yaḍirkum, lightened), and the meaning is the same.

﴿Indeed, Allah encompasses what they do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 121:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when you set out early from your family﴾, meaning: remember when you set out early (ghadwah) from your family, i.e., from the house of ʿĀʾishah. ﴿Assigning the believers to their positions﴾, i.e., settling the believers ﴿at stations for fighting﴾, meaning: placing them in the places and posts of battle. It is said: "bawwa'a fulānan makānа kadhā" (he settled so-and-so in such-and-such a place) when he placed him there. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Prophet (ﷺ) would designate for each one of the Muslims a place in [the battle] and station him there.

This was at the Battle of Uhud, and this verse, up to near the end of the surah, concerns the Battle of Uhud. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, i.e., All-Hearing of what the hypocrites said and All-Knowing of what they concealed; so it is in the mode of a warning. It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of what the believers said, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what they concealed; so it is in the mode of praise.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 122:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart﴾. He means: they intended and resolved. Al-hamm (resolve) means al-qasd (intention). As for the two groups, it is authentically related from Jabir that he said: by it he meant Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah. The account concerning this is what is related: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted his Companions about going out to fight at Uhud. Some of them advised going out and some advised remaining in Madinah, and he chose to go out. The army of the Muslims numbered a thousand, but Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul withdrew with a third of the army. Thereupon these two groups, Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah, resolved to return with them, but Allah, exalted is He, steadied them to continue on with him, so they did not return. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart﴾, that is: were about to become weak and cowardly. ﴿And Allah was their Protector﴾, that is: their Helper and the One who made them firm in the battle.

Jabir said: "We would not have wished that they should lose heart." And Allah said: ﴿And in Allah let the believers put their trust﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 123:

The words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr﴾ — He reminds them of His favour in granting them victory on the day of Badr. Badr is a place between Makkah and Madinah, and it was named Badr after the name of the location. It is said: it was named Badr after the name of a man, and it is said: after the name of a well. ﴿While you were humble﴾, meaning: few in number, for on the day of Badr they were three hundred and thirteen men. ʿAli said: "There was not a single horseman among us until al-Miqdad," and among them were seventy-seven men from the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the rest were from the Ansar (Helpers). The bearer of the banner of the Muhajirun was Amir al-Mu'minin ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, and the bearer of the banner of the Ansar was Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah.

At that time they had little weaponry, so Allah bestowed victory upon them, despite their small number and scant equipment. ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 124:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you"﴾. It is said that He meant by this the day of Badr; and it is said that He meant the day of Uhud. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The angels did not fight in battle except on the day of Badr."

That is, "Is it not enough for you" ﴿that your Lord should reinforce you﴾. Al-Imdad (reinforcement) is aiding an army with an army, and from it comes the word al-madad (reinforcement): ﴿with three thousand angels sent down﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 125:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Yes, if you are patient and mindful of God﴾, meaning: Yes, He promised you, if you are patient in facing the enemy, ﴿and mindful﴾, that is, you guard against opposing the Messenger, ﴿and they come upon you in this very rush﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and most of the exegetes said: its meaning is, ﴿in this very rush﴾ from their faces (wujuh, i.e. immediately). It was also said its meaning is: from their anger in this very moment, because they only returned to fight on the day of Uhud out of anger for the day of Badr.

﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand﴾. By this He did not intend five thousand other than the three thousand mentioned, because they agreed that the number of angels that day was five thousand. This is similar to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days?﴾, then He said after it: ﴿And He placed firm mountains upon it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days﴾, and He did not intend four days other than those two days, because He said after it: ﴿Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾. They agreed that the creation of all of it was in six days and not eight days; rather, He intended four days together with those two days. Thus is this also.

﴿Marked angels﴾ is read with the vowel fath on the waw (musawwimin), and the meaning is "those who marked themselves" (al-mu'allimin, i.e. distinguished by a sign). It is also read with kasra on the waw (musawwimin), so that the act of marking (al-taswim) is attributed to the angels; al-taswim is informing by means of a sign, and it derives from al-sawma, and al-sima is the sign. They differed concerning what the angels' sign was that day. 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr said: the angels were on horses, and yellow turbans were hung on them.

Al-Hasan said: they had white turbans let down behind their backs. Mujahid said: they had marked themselves with wool on the tails and forelocks of the horses; and this is a practice in the creation of the brave. And he (ﷺ) said: "Mark yourselves, for the angels have marked themselves."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 126:

Allah's saying: ﴿And Allah made it not but as good news for you﴾, i.e., as glad tidings for you, ﴿and that your hearts may be at rest thereby﴾, i.e., by His promise of victory. ﴿And victory is not but from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, meaning: do not take the victory as coming from the angels and the troops, but know that victory is from Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 127:

﴿That He might cut off a part of those who disbelieved﴾ That is: a portion of them. From this comes the word aṭrāf (limbs, extremities) of a person, because they are pieces of the self. Then, as for whoever applies the verse to the battle of Badr, that cutting off occurred among them on the day of Badr, for seventy of them were killed and seventy were taken captive, most of them being their leaders. And as for whoever applies the verse to the battle of Uhud, sixteen of them were killed, among them the standard-bearers. So victory was for the Muslims so long as they did not oppose the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When they opposed his command, victory departed from them.

His words: ﴿or subdue them﴾. Abū ʿUbayda said: that is, He destroys them (yuhlikuhum). It was also said that its meaning is: He disgraces them (yukhzīhim), and this is more sound. It was also said that its meaning is: or He throws them down (yaṣraʿahum). The kabt and kabt (kabb and kabt) mean to throw down upon the face. There is a fourth opinion concerning it: yakbitahum in the sense of yukbidahum (He grieves them), that is, that He makes them grieve until the grief reaches their livers (akbād). The Arabs call a grieving person "black of liver" (aswad al-kabid) due to the effect of grief upon him. [From this is] the saying of the poet:

(The enemies, and the livers are black...)

﴿so that they return disappointed﴾ That is: they do not attain what they hoped for. It is said: so-and-so returned from the expedition with disappointment (bi-l-khaybah) when he did not attain his hope.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 128:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You have no say whatsoever in the matter﴾. Al-Zuhri narrated from Salim, from his father Abdullah ibn Umar: "When ﴿You have no say whatsoever in the matter﴾ was revealed, he (ﷺ) gave up cursing them in the qunut."

And Anas narrated that on the day of Uhud his head was split open, his lower incisor was broken, and his face was bloodied. He would wipe the blood with his palm and say: "How can a people prosper who have dyed the face of their prophet?" Then there was revealed: ﴿You have no say whatsoever in the matter﴾.

It was also said: the Messenger of Allah wished to invoke a destructive supplication against them, so there was revealed: ﴿You have no say whatsoever in the matter﴾. That is because Allah, the Exalted, knew that among them were those who would embrace Islam [or repent] ﴿or He will turn to them in forgiveness or punish them﴾. It is governed by the same construction as His words: ﴿that He may cut off a part of those who disbelieve﴾. Its meaning: You have no say whatsoever in the matter; whether I turn to them in forgiveness or punish them, your affair follows My command. That is, if I turn to them in forgiveness, it is by My mercy, and if I punish them, it is by their wrongdoing.

If someone asks: what is the connection between ﴿or He will turn to them in forgiveness﴾ and His words ﴿You have no say whatsoever in the matter﴾? It is said: its meaning is: You have no say whatsoever in the matter, until He turns to them in forgiveness, or until He turns to them in forgiveness. A similar usage is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

(I said to her: do not let your eye weep, for we only strive for a kingdom or die and are excused)

That is: until we die and are excused. It may also be that it is in sequence with His words: ﴿that He may cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or humiliate them, or He will turn to them in forgiveness or punish them, for they are wrongdoers. You have no say whatsoever in the matter﴾.

And the matter is My matter in all of that.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 130:

O you who have believed, do not consume usury (al-riba), multiplied and multiplied again (﴿أَضْعَافًا مُضَاعَفَةً﴾). Usury (al-riba) has been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah, and He repeated its mention here for emphasis. "Multiplied manifold" (al-a'daf al-mudā'afah) refers to what they used to do: postponing the term of the debt in exchange for an increase in the principal.

﴿And fear Allah that you may prosper﴾. That is: be hopeful of success, meaning: whoever abandons usury, success is in it, and in the pursuit of usury is ruin.

And from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "No people perished except that usury and fornication became widespread among them." And also from him: "Much usury leads to scarcity."
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾. It is prepared for the disbelievers, for it is the abode of eternity for them.
﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy﴾. Meaning: be among those who hope for mercy.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 133:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness﴾, i.e., hasten to forgiveness ﴿from your Lord﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: its meaning is: hasten to repentance (tawbah), which is the cause of forgiveness. It was also said: it means: asking for forgiveness. And there is a strange (gharib) opinion that it refers to the first takbir (the opening takbir of prayer).

﴿And a garden whose width is like the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., its breadth is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth.

[And in a report: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: if Paradise's width is the heavens and the earth, then where is the Fire?" He, peace be upon him, said: "When the night comes, where does the day go? And when the day comes, where does the night go?"] And its meaning, and God knows best, is that it is wherever God wills.

If it is said: God, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised﴾, and by what we are promised He means Paradise. If it is in the heaven, how can its width be the heavens and the earth? It is said: the gate of Paradise is in the heaven, and its width is the heavens and the earth, as He has informed.

It was also said: He meant by it on the Day of Resurrection, for God will increase it, so that its width becomes the heavens and the earth when the heavens and the earth are joined one to another. As for its length, none knows it except God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 134:

﴿Prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), who spend in ease and in hardship﴾ That is: in (ease and hardship) ﴿and who restrain their anger﴾. Kazm al-ghayz (restraining anger) is that a person is filled with anger, yet prevents it from taking effect, from the expression "kazama al-ba'ir bi-jirratihi" (the camel held its cud), when it returns it to its inside. And in a report: "Whoever is filled with anger, and restrains it, God will give him the choice among the dark-eyed maidens (al-hur al-'in)."

﴿and who pardon people﴾. It has been said: pardoning the slaves (mamalik) for bad manners; and it has been said: in general, pardoning all people. ﴿And God loves the good-doers (al-muhsinin)﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 135:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves﴾ refers to what falls short of fornication: kissing, embracing, touching, pressing against one another, and the like. ﴿They remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins.﴾ The occasion of revelation of the verse is what has been related: that a man in Medina, called Nabhan, was a date merchant. A woman came to him to buy dates from him, and he was attracted by her beauty and kissed her. Then he remembered Allah, regretted, and sought forgiveness; so the verse was revealed.

﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah﴾, that is: they remember the threat of Allah. ﴿And seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah? — and do not persist in what they have done while they know.﴾ Persistence (al-israr) is remaining upon disobedience without repentance. So His saying, ﴿and do not persist﴾, means: and do not continue or go on ﴿in what they have done while they know﴾ that Allah's forgiveness of sin is not too great for Him, however much the sin may be. It has been related from Ma'bad ibn Subayhah that he said: "I prayed behind Uthman, and when he finished his prayer he said: 'Indeed Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿and do not persist in what they have done﴾, and I have prayed without ablution, forgetfully, and here I am performing ablution.'" So he went and performed ablution (and washed) and repeated the prayer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 136:

﴿Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord, and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; and excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾ In this verse He mentions the reward of those who remember (Allah) and those who seek forgiveness, and reports concerning seeking forgiveness (istighfar) have been transmitted. Among them is what is related with a raised (marfu') chain: "One who seeks forgiveness does not persist in sin, even if he returns to it seventy times in a day."

Asma' ibn al-Hakam al-Fazari related from Ali that he said: "When I hear a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefits me by it as He wills; and when I hear it from someone else, I make him swear by it, and when he swears, I believe him." And Abu Bakr, who is truthful, narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant commits a sin, then performs ablution, prays two rak'ahs, and seeks forgiveness from Allah, except that Allah forgives him."

Know that seeking forgiveness is an ease for this Ummah, for those before us, when one of them committed a sin, it was written at his door (as an instruction): "Cut off such-and-such a limb from yourself," and it was necessary for him to do so. Allah, may He be exalted, has freed this Ummah from sins through seeking forgiveness, as an honour for them and as facilitation upon them.

Ibn al-Mu'tazz was asked: "If Allah, may He be exalted, has vast forgiveness, and His mercy encompasses everything, what prevents Him from showing mercy to the disbeliever?" He said: "Indeed His mercy does not overcome His wisdom."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 137:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, there have passed before you precedents⁠—﴾. Ibn Mas'ud read: "qad madat" (there have passed), which has the same meaning as "khalat" (have passed). The sunnah (a customary way, a path of conduct followed) is the path that is followed, whether for good or for evil.

He (ﷺ) said concerning the Magians: "Treat them as you would treat the People of the Book" (sanna bihim sunnat ahl al-kitab), and this was an evil for them. And the poet said:

(And indeed those who were slain at al-Taff from the family of Hashim... they set an example, and they established the example for the noble ones)

Ibn 'Abbas said: the sunan of those who came before you, and these are the acts of God's retribution against the disbelievers. Another said: they are the signs and the traces that existed. The essential meaning is that they are the ways of God regarding the disbelievers, in killing them, taking them captive, ruining their dwellings, and the like. Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿Precedents have passed before you﴾, meaning: people of precedents (ahl sunan). ﴿So travel through the earth and see how was the end of those who denied﴾.

This is a tafsir passage with a Qur'anic quotation, a report from al-Sha'bi, and a short explanation. Translating faithfully.

**The Exalted's saying: ﴿This is a clear statement for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing.﴾** Al-Sha'bi said: "A clarification from blindness, a guidance from misguidance, and an admonition from ignorance." As for *bayan* (clarification), it is the manifestation of the meaning of speech; and *mau'iza* (admonition) is calling to the truth through encouragement (*targhib*) and warning (*tarhib*).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 139:

The Most High said: ﴿And do not be weak, nor grieve﴾. That is: do not become feeble, do not become cowardly, and do not grieve, ﴿and you will have the upper hand﴾. That is: the final outcome and victory will be yours.
