It was said: He only said ﴿and you will have the upper hand﴾ because the Muslims were on the mountain while the polytheists were at the foot of the mountain. And His words ﴿if you are believers﴾ mean: do not be weak if you are believers, because faith increases strength, so it does not produce weakness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 140:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If a wound (qarh) touches you﴾. It is recited with a fatha on the qaf and with a damma on it. Al-Farra' said: al-qarh (with a fatha) is the wound, and al-qarh is the pain. Al-Kisa'i said: they are two expressions for one meaning. Most scholars hold the first view. His saying, ﴿If a wound touches you﴾, is addressed to the Muslims regarding what touched them on the Day of Uhud, ﴿then a wound like it has touched the people (al-qawm)﴾, meaning: the disbelievers were touched on the Day of Badr (with a wound) like what touched you on the Day of Uhud.

﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾: at one time victory belongs to the Muslims over the disbelievers, and at another time to the disbelievers over the Muslims. Al-Zajjaj said: victory (al-dawla) may belong to the Muslims over the disbelievers, and it has indeed belonged to the disbelievers over the Muslims when they opposed the Messenger's command. But if they do not oppose his command, victory will always belong to the Muslims, based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers will be the victors﴾, and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the party of Allah will be the victorious﴾.

﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "and that Allah may test (liyubli) those who believe," but the well-known reading is ﴿and that He may know (liya'lam)﴾. If someone says: what is the meaning of His saying, ﴿and that Allah may know those who believe﴾, when He always knows them? It is said: its meaning is that He may know those who are patient in jihad in the places of jihad, so that He deals with them as one who tests them, and so He makes them known. Knowledge of jihad in the places of jihad occurs only after jihad has taken place. It is also said: the first knowledge is knowledge of the unseen, while ﴿and that He may know﴾ means knowledge of witnessing, and the occurrence and the recompense are based on knowledge of occurrence, not on knowledge of the unseen.

﴿And that He may take from among you martyrs, and Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾. That is, He did not give the disbelievers the upper hand on the Day of Uhud out of love for them; rather, so that He might test you and make you martyrs.

**Al-Sam'ani's Tafsir al-Quran on surah 3, verse 141:**

His words, exalted is He: ﴿That Allah may purify those who believe﴾. All of this follows the pattern of His words: ﴿That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieved﴾, (and likewise) His words: ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾.

As for *tamhis* (purification through testing or refining): it has been said that it means [*takhlis*] (sifting out, purifying), and this is the view of al-Hasan. Mujahid said it means *ibtila'* (trial, testing). The true meaning of *tamhis* is purification from sins. The Arabs say, "*Mahhasa* 'anna dhunubana," meaning: He purified us from our sins.

﴿And destroy the disbelievers﴾. The meaning of the verse is: if they kill you, that is a purification for you; and if you kill them, that is their destruction and annihilation.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strove, and made evident the patient?﴾ That is, "Did you (think, ʾa-ḥasibtum)" — the interrogative hamza here introduces a rebuke. ﴿While Allah has not yet known those of you who strove⦆ — that is, while Allah has not yet known those among you in whom striving (jihad) has actually occurred, ﴿and known the patient﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 143:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And you had certainly been wishing for death﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse is that those among the Muslims who stayed away from the battle of Badr said, when the battle of Badr had ended: "If only we had a day like it, so that we might fight, be killed, and attain martyrdom." Then, when the day of Uhud came, they fled and retreated, and the verse was revealed.

﴿And you had certainly been wishing for death﴾: that is, the cause of death, which is jihad, since it is not permissible to wish for death at the hands of the disbelievers. ﴿Before you met it﴾: that is, before you encountered its cause, which is jihad. ﴿Then you have certainly seen it while you were looking on﴾. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿while you were looking on﴾, when He has already said ﴿you have certainly seen it﴾? It is said: the seeing may be meant as knowing, so He said ﴿while you were looking on﴾ to make clear that the intended meaning of "seeing" here is reflection (tafakkur). This was said by al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash, a grammarian). It is also said: He said it only for emphasis. It is also said: its meaning is: "while you were looking on at Muhammad."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 144:

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him﴾. The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that when the Muslims at the Battle of Uhud were defeated and killing befell them, the Shaytan (may he receive what he deserves) cried out: "Verily, Muhammad has been killed!" The Muslims said: "Seek safe conduct for us from Abu Sufyan." And those in whose hearts was hypocrisy said: "Return to your former religion, for Muhammad has been killed." Then there was revealed: ﴿Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ That is, he remains upon his message and prophethood whether he dies or is killed; so why would you turn back on your heels? ﴿And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all﴾, that is, he harms only himself. ﴿And Allah will reward the grateful﴾.

It is also narrated that Anas ibn al-Nadr, when he heard the Shaytan's saying, "Verily, Muhammad has been killed," drew his sword and headed toward the disbelievers, saying: "If Muhammad has been killed, then what remains of [life] for us? Fight on as he fought, and die as he died." So he fought until he was killed.

Ka'b ibn Malik said: "I was the first to see the Messenger of Allah on the day of Uhud after the Shaytan's cry. I recognised him by his eyes beneath the helmet, so I said: 'This is the Messenger of Allah, alive!' He gestured to me to be silent."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 145:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by the permission of Allah﴾. Its implied sense is: "And a soul would not die except by the permission of Allah, by His decree and His destiny." ﴿A decree with a specified term﴾. Its implied sense is: "He has decreed a decree with a specified term."

(And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof.) If it is said: "We see one who desires this world and is not given it?" It is said: its meaning is that what has been decreed for him of the reward of this world is not withheld from him because of his disbelief.

﴿And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof.﴾ If it is said: "Is the reward of the Hereafter given merely by desiring it?" It is said: its meaning is: "And whoever desires it by action." This is like saying: "So-and-so desires Paradise," meaning: he works for Paradise. ﴿And We will reward the grateful.﴾ That is, the believers. 'Ali - may Allah be pleased with him - said: "Abu Bakr is the imam of the grateful," meaning: the imam of the believers, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 146:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How many a prophet [fought and] there fought with him many devoted servants (rabbiyyun)﴾. That is: how many a prophet was killed. Jarir said:

(How many in the valleys is a friend who sees me, if I am struck, he is the one struck.)

ʿIkrimah said: this is a complete pause (waqf tamm), and its meaning is: how many a prophet was killed while his companions were with him.

﴿So they did not weaken for what afflicted them in the way of Allah﴾, that is, they did not become cowardly, ﴿nor were they weakened, nor did they submit﴾, that is, they did not abase themselves and did not yield. Al-Hasan said: no prophet was ever killed in a battle at all; rather the meaning of the verse is: how many a prophet had many devoted servants fight alongside him and be killed. As for the other reading, "qatala" (fought), its meaning is clear. As for al-Rabbiyyun (the devoted servants, sing. rabbi, a term for a godly scholar or worshipper), Ibn Mas'ud said: they are thousands. It was also said: they are ten thousand. Al-Hasan said: al-Rabbiyyun, from among the scholars, is derived from "al-rabb" (the Lord), because they are upon the religion of the Lord and His path.

His saying, exalted is He: {And Allah loves the patient}

"And their saying was only that they said: 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins (dhunubana)', meaning the minor sins (al-saghair), ﴿and our excesses in our affair﴾, meaning the major sins (al-kaba'ir), ﴿and make firm our feet and help us against the disbelieving people.﴾"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 148:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾ means: (al-nusrah) victory and booty.

﴿And the good reward of the Hereafter﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is that Allah will settle the Prophet and his Companions in domes of pearl and ruby until He judges between the creatures. It was also said: the good reward of the Hereafter is that He will recompense them for their deeds and increase them from His bounty. ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers﴾.

O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will return you to your heels, and you will turn back as losers. (Q. 3:149)

Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers. (Q. 3:150)

Al-Sam'ani's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an):

The words of the Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ — meaning: the Jews and the Christians — ﴿they will return you to your heels﴾ — meaning: to Judaism and Christianity.

It is also said that by this He meant the hypocrites who said on the day of Uhud: "Return to your former religion, for Muhammad has been killed." This is the meaning of His words, the Most High: ﴿they will return you to your heels, and you will turn back as losers﴾ — that is, defrauded (maghbunin). ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾

O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will return you to your heels, and you will turn back as losers. (Q. 3:149)

Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers. (Q. 3:150)

Al-Sam'ani's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an):

The words of the Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ — meaning: the Jews and the Christians — ﴿they will return you to your heels﴾ — meaning: to Judaism and Christianity.

It is also said that by this He meant the hypocrites who said on the day of Uhud: "Return to your former religion, for Muhammad has been killed." This is the meaning of His words, the Most High: ﴿they will return you to your heels, and you will turn back as losers﴾ — that is, defrauded (maghbunin). ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 151:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: fear (al-ru'b). He said: "I was given victory through terror over a distance of a month's journey." ﴿Because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority﴾, meaning: because of their association of partners with Allah, for which He had not sent down any proof. Al-sultan (authority) means proof. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Lost is my authority (sultaniyah)﴾, meaning: my proof.

﴿And their refuge is the Fire﴾, meaning: their place is the Fire. ﴿And wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: when the defeat befell the Muslims on the day of Uhud, and killing occurred among them, the polytheists consulted among themselves and agreed to return to fighting, so as to annihilate Muhammad and his companions. Allah, exalted is He, then cast terror into their hearts, so they fled on their faces, not turning back for anything, until they reached Makkah. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 152:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾, meaning: His promise to you of victory and support was fulfilled. Support had been granted to the Muslims at the beginning of the day of Uhud. ﴿When you were killing them by His permission﴾, meaning: you were killing them by the decree and predestination of Allah. Al-Halsu (the killing) is from the same root, and from it is the saying of the poet:

(The swords cut them down as the flame of fire rises up in the thicket of the harvested reed.)

﴿Until, when you lost courage﴾, meaning: you became cowardly, ﴿and disputed about the matter﴾. Its construction is: until when you lost courage, you disputed about the matter, and the "waw" is extra; this was said by al-Farra'. It was also said that there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, and its construction is: until when you disputed about the matter, you lost courage. ﴿And you disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾, meaning: the victory and the spoils of war.

﴿Among you are those who desire the world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾, because they differed, as we will mention. ﴿Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾, meaning: He restrained your hands from them in order to examine you. It was also said: to bring affliction upon you. ﴿And certainly He pardoned you; and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾ The story concerning this is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw in his dream that he had put on a strong coat of mail when the polytheists descended upon Uhud; so he interpreted it as (meaning) Medina, and he consulted his companions about going out to Uhud. They said: "This is a town that no one has entered against us without being attacked, and no one has come to it without our going out to meet them." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) put on two coats of mail, placed the helmet on his head, and went out. They regretted it and realized that his intention had been to remain (in Medina). They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we follow your opinion," and they asked him to return if he wished. He said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet, when he has put on his armour, to take it off until he fights, or until Allah judges."

He set out with a thousand men, but Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul [and his companions] withdrew with a third of the army, three hundred men, and seven hundred remained. When he reached Uhud, he sent a group of archers and seated them at a place on a mountain where an ambush was feared, and he appointed over them Abdullah ibn Jubayr al-Ansari.

﴿...the world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter; then He turned you away from them to test you; and certainly He pardoned you; and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

Then the fighting with the polytheists began; the Muslims gained the upper hand, killed a number of their leaders, and they fled. The victory appeared for the Muslims, and they pursued them for the spoils. When the archers saw this, they said: "The polytheists have been defeated, and victory has appeared; let us follow them and take booty." Abdullah ibn Jubayr said: "Do not leave this place, for the Messenger of Allah commanded you to remain in this place; so remain in it." They disagreed with him, most of them left, and Abdullah ibn Jubayr remained with a few of his companions.

When the place of the ambush was left empty of the archers, Khalid ibn al-Walid came out at them from the ambush and attacked them with killing. Abdullah ibn Jubayr was martyred, along with those who remained with him. The polytheists returned to fighting, slaughter fell upon the Muslims, seventy of them were killed, and the rest fled. Only a few remained with the Messenger of Allah. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾, meaning: at the beginning, with victory and support, ﴿when you were killing them by His permission, until when you lost courage and disputed about the matter﴾, meaning: those archers who disagreed. ﴿And you disobeyed﴾, meaning: you disobeyed the Messenger and opposed his command ﴿after He had shown you﴾, meaning: after Allah had shown you ﴿what you love﴾ of victory. ﴿Among you are those who desire the world﴾: they are those who went for the spoils. ﴿And among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾: those who remained steadfast with Abdullah ibn Jubayr.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "We did not know that any of us desired the world until Allah revealed this verse."

﴿Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾, meaning: in the second encounter, when the polytheists returned. This is evidence for the People of the Sunnah that the actions of servants are created, since Allah attributed the defeat of the Muslims to Himself although the act occurred from them, saying: ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿when you were climbing﴾. It is also read with a fatha on the ta' and the ayn. Al-Ismad is walking on level ground, and as-su'ud is walking on elevated ground.

The address is to the Muslims who fled,

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 153:**

By His saying: ﴿When you were climbing up and not turning aside for anyone﴾, meaning: you were not ascending [in fear] and not turning your attention to anyone. Then some said: ﴿by "anyone" is meant﴾ the Messenger; and others said: its meaning is: you did not turn aside for any of the people.

﴿While the Messenger was calling you from your rear﴾, meaning: at the rear of the army. He was calling them: "O servants of God, come to me, come to me, I am the Messenger of God." But they did not turn to him, and they went on.

﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾, meaning: He repaid you. Then they differed. Some said: the first grief was the killing and the defeat that befell the Muslims, and the second grief was the rumour from the words of Satan: "Muhammad has been killed." It was also said: the first grief was the killing and the defeat, and the second grief was the missing of victory over the enemy.

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that they caused the Messenger grief by disobeying his command, so God, exalted is He, repaid them with that grief: the grief of the killing and the defeat. He called it a reward only because He placed it in the position of a reward, as He said: ﴿So give them the tidings of a painful punishment﴾, where He called the punishment "tidings" because He placed it in the position of tidings. ﴿That you may not grieve over what escapes you, nor over what befalls you﴾, namely the killing and the defeat. God forbade them from grieving over anything with which He tested them, and promised a reward for it. ﴿And God is Aware of what you do﴾.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security﴾. It was said: "Amn" (security) and "amana" (a state of safety) have the same meaning. It was also said: [the word] is used together with the removal of the cause of fear. Here, however, He said: ﴿security, drowsiness overcoming a group of you﴾. It was said: there is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in it, and its sense is "drowsiness as security." It was also said: it is correct in its arrangement. The meaning of the verse is that Allah, the Exalted, willed to distinguish the believers from the hypocrites. So He caused drowsiness to fall upon the believers as security for them, until they felt safe, and He did not cause it to fall upon the hypocrites, so they remained in fear.

Abu Talha said: Allah, the Exalted, caused drowsiness to fall upon us while we were beneath the shield.

It was also said: drowsiness fell upon them to the point that swords would slip from their hands. Likewise, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and al-Zubayr reported about that drowsiness, just as Abu Talha reported.

Al-Zubayr said: When Allah caused drowsiness to fall upon us, we heard Mu'tib ibn Qushayr saying: "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here." I was as though in sleep, hearing [him]. This is His saying: ﴿a group of you﴾, meaning the believers, ﴿and a group who were concerned about themselves﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah, saying: "Do we have any say in the matter?"﴾. He said: ﴿Say: "Indeed, the matter is entirely with Allah." They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you﴾.

Then He explained that, saying: ﴿They say: "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here." Say: "Even if you had been in your houses, those decreed to be killed would have gone out to their places of death."﴾

That is: those for whom fighting was decreed went out to their places of falling in death. In this there is evidence that the appointed term of killing and of death is one, as Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah) have said.

His saying, the Exalted: (And that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts, and Allah is Knowing of the contents of the breasts).

.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 155:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met﴾. He means: those among the Muslims who fled on the day of Uhud. When the defeat befell the Muslims, most of them fled, and there remained with the Messenger of Allah only fourteen men: seven of the Muhajirun (emigrants) and seven of the Ansar (helpers). It is also said: thirteen, six of the Muhajirun, namely Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Talhah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.

In the first report: the seventh was al-Zubayr, and Talhah was the most effective in inflicting harm upon the disbelievers that day.

It is also said that the day of Uhud belonged to Talhah. It is said that he was a shield for the Messenger of Allah, and that his hand was struck and became paralysed, and it remained so.

As for Sa'd, he was an archer, and he used to shoot in front of the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah would say to him: "Shoot, may my father and mother be your ransom."

As for those who fled, some of them reached Madinah, among them Uthman, and some of them returned along the road, among them Umar. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿It was only that Satan caused them to slip﴾, i.e., sought their slip. It is said: "istaʿjalahu" (he sought to hasten him), meaning he sought his haste. Its meaning is that Satan caused them to slip until they fled.

His saying ﴿because of some of what they had earned﴾ means: because of their opposition to the Messenger. ﴿And Allah has already pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: The cause of their flight was that Satan whispered to them: "Indeed, you have sins"; so they disliked being killed before they repented of their sins. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿It was only that Satan caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. And Allah has already pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾.

It is related: "A man came to Ibn Umar, and it is said: to Ibn Abbas, and the more correct is to Ibn Abbas, and said: Was not Uthman absent from Badr? He said: Yes. He said: Was he not absent from the Pledge of al-Ridwan? He said: Yes. He said: Did he not flee on the day of Uhud? He said: Yes.

The man said: Allahu Akbar!

Ibn Abbas understood that he intended to belittle him, so he called him over and said: As for the day of Badr, the Prophet had left him behind to care for his daughter, who was ill, and he said to him: "You have the reward of one who was present, and a share of what he obtained; and he is a man of Badr by the words of the Messenger."

As for the Pledge of al-Ridwan, the Messenger had sent Uthman to Makkah as an envoy, and had he had anyone among them in the valley more honoured than him, he would have sent that person. When he gave the pledge to them, the Messenger of Allah struck his left hand upon his right and said: "This is the hand of Uthman, and this is my hand." As for his fleeing on the day of Uhud, Allah has pardoned him, and there is no fault in anything Allah has pardoned."

Section

"As for what befell the Messenger of Allah on the day of Uhud: his helmet which was on his head was broken, his face was bleeding, and his front tooth was broken. He came to Madinah, and Fatimah used to wash his face, while Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, brought water in a shield, and the blood would only increase, until she burned a mat, and when it became ash, they placed it on the wound, and the blood stopped."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 156:

The words of God Most High: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: the hypocrites (al-munafiqin), ﴿and say to their brothers when they travel through the land﴾. He intended: their brothers by lineage, not in religion. ﴿When they travel through the land﴾, i.e., they journey. ﴿Or are raiders﴾, plural of ghazi (raider, one who goes out to fight). ﴿If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed﴾. This is the statement of al-Mu'tabb ibn Qushayr, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and Jadd ibn Qays. ﴿That God may make that a regret in their hearts. And God gives life and causes death, and God is Seeing of what you do﴾.

Almighty God's words: ﴿And if you are killed in the way of God, or die﴾ — that is, if you go forth and are killed, or if you do not go forth and die — ﴿surely forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what they amass﴾ — of the world — and seek life for its sake.

And if you die or are killed, to Allah you will surely be gathered. (Qur'an 3:158)

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you die or are killed, to Allah you will surely be gathered﴾ means: however you leave this world, your gathering is to Allah, the Exalted.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 159:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So by a mercy from Allah﴾, meaning: by mercy. The "mā" here is a *ṣila* (a redundant particle that adds emphasis without changing the meaning). ﴿You were gentle with them﴾. This is the attribute of the believers, and the Prophet said: "The believers are easygoing and gentle, like the camel with a sore nose: if it is led, it follows, and if it is made to kneel on a rock, it kneels."

﴿And had you been harsh﴾, meaning coarse and rude, ﴿hard-hearted﴾, meaning cruel of heart, ﴿they would have dispersed from around you﴾, meaning they would have scattered.

﴿So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter﴾. *Mushāwara* (consultation) is the extraction of opinion. Consultation was permitted for the Prophet in worldly affairs. As for matters of religion, the ruling is detailed:

- If the matter involves two options, both of which are permissible, consultation is allowed, as when he consulted them about the captives of Badr, where either killing or ransom was permissible.
- The second case concerns matters established by explicit text, such as fasting and prayer, where consultation is not permitted.
- The third case concerns a matter on which there is no explicit text. Here it depends on whether his *ijtihad* (independent legal judgment) was valid. If his *ijtihad* was valid, consulting him is permitted; otherwise it is not.

Why did he consult them? al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: so that they would be emulated and his practice would be followed. This is also the view of Sufyān al-Thawrī. Qatāda said: to comfort their hearts.

﴿And when you have resolved, then rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: do not rely upon consultation, but rely upon Allah alone. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him﴾.

﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? So let the believers put their trust in Allah.﴾ Al-khidhlan (forsaking): refraining from giving support when it is needed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 161:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a prophet to deceive (yaghull)﴾ are read in two ways. Whoever reads it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the ghayn, its meaning is: that he should betray (yakhun).

Ibn 'Abbas said: The occasion of the revelation of the verse was that on the day of Badr a red woollen cloak (qatifa hamra') went missing, and some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah said: "The Messenger has taken it." So there was revealed the words: ﴿It is not for a prophet to deceive﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Its meaning is: It is not for a prophet to conceal anything of the revelation and to betray in it.

There is a third view: "The Prophet had sent out scouts (talai'), and they asked him to give them something of the spoils, so he did not give them anything; then there was revealed the words: ﴿It is not for a prophet to deceive﴾." Qatada said: [it means] that he should not be betrayed by them, i.e., do not betray him. It was also said that its meaning is: that he should be attributed with ghulul (embezzlement of spoils), and it was said that its meaning is: that he should bring a ghull (shackle/fetter) [i.e., come with a chain], and this is a strange meaning compared with the first reading. Al-ghulul (embezzlement, "ghulul") means betrayal; al-ghull means rancour (hiqd); and al-ghalal means the water that flows among the trees, and from it is the saying of the poet:

(The torrents played with it, so its water became / a flowing stream [yukhallil] among the roots of the castor-oil plant)

In a report, the Prophet said: "Three things against which the heart of a Muslim man does not harbour ghull: sincerity of deed for the sake of Allah, counsel to the rulers of affairs, and adherence to the community of the Muslims, for their supplication surrounds them from behind."

﴿And whoever embezzles﴾, i.e., whoever betrays, ﴿will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection﴾. It is said: he will bring what he embezzled exactly as it was on the Day of Resurrection, and that is the meaning of his words, as related from him: "I will surely find one of you on the Day of Resurrection with a horse on his neck which neighs, which he has embezzled, and he will say: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Indeed I have conveyed.' I will surely find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a sheep on his neck which bleats, which he has embezzled, and he will say: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Indeed I have conveyed.' I will surely find one of you on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck which roars, which he has embezzled, and he will say: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Indeed I have conveyed.'"

The second view: he meant by it: he will come bearing the sin of what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. In a report: a man was in charge of the baggage of the Messenger of Allah, and he was martyred, and the people said: "He is in Paradise." The Prophet said: "He is in the Fire." So they searched, and it was found that he had embezzled a cloak from the spoils.

﴿Then every soul will be paid in full for what it earned﴾, i.e., the recompense of what it earned; the recompense is implied in it. ﴿And they will not be wronged.﴾

Almighty God says: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of God﴾, meaning: one who abandons embezzlement (al-ghulul), ﴿like one who has incurred wrath from God﴾, meaning: through embezzlement. It has also been said that its meaning is: Is one who follows the pleasure of God by complying with the Messenger, like one who has incurred wrath from God by opposing the Messenger? ﴿And his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾.

The Exalted said: ﴿They are in degrees with Allah﴾. Mujahid said: "They have degrees with Allah," meaning the believers. Another commentator said: its implied meaning is, "They are possessors of degrees with Allah," meaning the believers and the hypocrites. So the believers are possessors of lofty degrees, and the hypocrites are possessors of base degrees. A similar usage is the words of the poet:

(I set myself up as a target for death that besets them, my men, or are they the courses of the torrents?)

That is, they are possessors of the courses of the torrents. ﴿And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do﴾.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 164:

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favour upon the believers﴾, meaning: He bestowed favour. Al-mann (favour) is the blessing (ni'mah), and al-mann also means cutting off. From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For them is a reward never cut off﴾, meaning: never cut off. The blessing was named mannah because it is cut off from afflictions and hardships.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When He sent among them a Messenger from themselves﴾. It has been said: this refers specifically to the Arabs, because the Messenger was sent from the descendants of Isma'il to the Arabs. It has also been said: it is general in its application to all mankind, for he was sent as a human being like them.

The point of the favour in His sending of a Messenger to the Arabs from among themselves is that it was an honour for them, since the Messenger was sent from among them. Also, the Qur'an was revealed in the tongue of the Arabs, since the Messenger was an Arab, and learning it was easier for them, because it was closer to their understanding. So the favour lies in the ease it gave them. Furthermore, since he grew up among them, and they knew his truthfulness and trustworthiness, and he was unlettered like them, not knowing how to write and knowing nothing, and he did not travel, then he brought a Book that tells of past generations and the stories of the earlier peoples, and that agrees with the Scriptures revealed before him, it was closer to their hearts, and so the path of faith became easy for them.

And His saying: ﴿He recites to them His verses and purifies them﴾, meaning: He bears witness to the purification of all other nations, and makes them pure. It has been said: He purifies them from sins. ﴿And teaches them the Book﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. ﴿And the wisdom﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: the understanding (fiqh) and the laws (shara'i'). Others said: al-hikmah (wisdom) is the Sunnah. ﴿And indeed they were before in manifest error﴾, meaning: they were before this only in manifest error.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 165:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Or when a calamity afflicted you, though you had inflicted twice as much [in return]﴾ — meaning, the day of Uhud — ﴿you had inflicted twice as much﴾ — meaning, the day of Badr. The verse was revealed to console the believers. That is because on the day of Uhud seventy of the Muslims were killed, while on the day of Badr the Muslims had inflicted upon them seventy killed and seventy captured, which makes twice their number. Thus He made the captives equal to the killed, since the slain and the captives of the day of Badr were double the slain of Uhud.

﴿You said, "From where is this?"﴾ — from where is this? ﴿Say, "It is from yourselves."﴾ — meaning, by your opposing the Messenger. And it is related from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said, regarding the Exalted's words ﴿Say, "It is from yourselves"﴾, that it means by your choice of ransom. That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) gave the Muslims, on the day of Badr, the choice regarding the captives between killing and ransom, and said to them: "If you choose ransom, a number equal to them will be struck down from among you in the coming year." So they chose ransom, saying: "We will strengthen ourselves with it against the enemy, and some of us will be martyred." That is His saying: ﴿Say, "It is from yourselves"﴾ — meaning, by your choice. This is also the view of ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him). ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things Powerful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 166:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever afflicted you on the day the two hosts met﴾, meaning the day of Uhud, ﴿was by the permission of Allah﴾, that is, by the knowledge of Allah.

It is related that when the polytheists encamped at Uhud, he (ﷺ) saw in his dream that cows were being slaughtered, and he interpreted this as meaning that some of his companions would be martyred. He also saw that his sword Dhu al-Fiqar had broken, and he interpreted this as meaning the killing of Hamzah. He saw that a dusty-colored ram had been killed, and he interpreted this as meaning the killing of the champion of the disbelievers. On the day of Uhud, their champion, Uthman ibn Talhah al-Abdari, of the Banu Abd al-Dar, was killed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 167:

﴿And that He may make known those who believe, and that He may make known those who acted hypocritically.﴾ He means: knowledge of witnessing (ʿilm al-mushahada), even though their knowledge is knowledge of the unseen (ʿilm al-ghayb).

﴿And it was said to them: "Come, fight in the way of Allah, or defend."﴾ The one who said this was ʿAbd Allah ibn Haram, Abu Jabir. He said to the hypocrites: "Fight in the way of Allah, and even if you do not fight for the sake of religion, then defend against (for) the family and the sanctuary."

﴿They said: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would certainly follow you."﴾ So they turned back, saying: "There is no fighting, there is no fighting," until the Muslims would be weakened. ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith.﴾ He means: after their turning back and that statement of theirs; because previously they were among the believers outwardly, even though they were hypocrites inwardly. When they parted from the believers, they became nearer to disbelief than to faith.

﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts, and Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 168:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who said of their brothers﴾ means: by lineage, not by religion. They were the hypocrites (al-munafiqun). They said to the Muslims: "If they had stayed behind, they would not have been killed," just as we were not killed. That is His saying: ﴿Those who said of their brothers, while they sat at home, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say: "Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful."﴾ It means: if you are able to ward off being killed, and you are able to ward off death, then ward off death from yourselves. Al-darʾ (warding off) means repelling, and from it is the saying of the poet:

("I say, when I have pulled back her reins for her, / Is this ever your religion, and my religion?")

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 169:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: when the Companions of the Messenger of Allah were martyred on the Day of Uhud, people would say: "So-and-so has died; so-and-so has died." Then the saying of Allah, exalted is He, was revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾. It has been said that its meaning is: they will be alive on the Day of Resurrection. However, this is weak, because no special distinction would remain for them in it. The more correct view is that it is in the sense of what has been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "The spirits of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds, they graze from the fruits of Paradise" – and in another narration: "they eat" – and in another narration: "they roam in Paradise and then return to its rivers" – "then they take shelter in lamps of gold suspended from the Throne." Muslim related it in his Sahih, and he added: "Allah, exalted is He, looks down upon them with a look, and says: 'Ask of Me.' They say: 'What should we ask, when You have given us this?' He says: 'Ask of Me.' They say: 'What should we ask, when You have given us this?' He says: 'Ask of Me.' They say: 'We ask that You return us to the world so that we may be killed in Your way a second time.'" The hadith...

And in a third narration: "The Prophet saw Jabir sad, and his father 'Abd Allah ibn Haram had been killed on the Day of Uhud. He said: 'Why do I see you sad? Allah, exalted is He, has not spoken to anyone except from behind a veil, but He spoke to your father face to face.' He said: 'Ask of Me.'" The hadith...

It is also related that "the martyrs of Uhud said: 'Who will convey to our Prophet and our brothers what we have reached?' Allah, exalted is He, said: 'I will convey it to them' – and in another narration: 'I am your Messenger' – and He revealed this verse."

{Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for}

Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and they receive good tidings concerning those who have not yet joined them from behind them (﴿ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم﴾). It has been said that its meaning is: He delivers to them a book containing the names of their brothers who will be martyred after them, and so they rejoice on their account.

And His saying: ﴿And they receive good tidings concerning those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾, when it was possible for them to join them. There is another view concerning it: that the martyrs say, "Would that our brothers were struck as we were struck, so that they might arrive at what we have arrived at." That is His saying: ﴿And they receive good tidings concerning those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾, i.e., that there is no fear upon them ﴿nor shall they grieve﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 171:

﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and a bounty﴾. It was said: by "blessing" (ni'mah) is meant sufficiency (qadr al-kifayah), and by "bounty" (fadl) is meant what exceeds sufficiency. Its meaning is: it is not restricted for them, but rather it is extended in giving. It was also said: the mention of "bounty" is for emphasis of the blessing. ﴿And that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited:

"Wallahu la yudi'u ajr al-mu'minin" (وَالله لَا يضيع أجر الْمُؤمنِينَ).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 172:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who responded to God and the Messenger﴾. It is said: the occasion of the revelation of the verse was that when Abu Sufyan returned to Makkah on the day of Uhud, the disbelievers said to one another on the road: "Let us turn back and uproot Muhammad and his Companions." This reached the Messenger of God, and he said: "Who will volunteer to go out?" Seventy men volunteered, among them Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr.

'Aishah had said to 'Urwah: "Your two parents are among those who responded to God and the Messenger," meaning that Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr were among the seventy. They went out to Hamra' al-Asad, [which is] eight miles from Madinah. When they arrived, [they found that] God had cast terror into the hearts of the polytheists, and they had already gone on to Makkah.

Ibn 'Abbas said (another view): when Abu Sufyan wanted to return on the day of Uhud, he said: "Our appointment with you is next year at Badr." Then it did not happen for him to go out the following year, and the Messenger of God went out to Badr with his Companions for the appointment. Those are the ones who responded to God and the Messenger.

﴿After the wound had afflicted them﴾, meaning: the pain on the day of Uhud. ﴿For those among them who did good﴾ by responding to the Messenger, ﴿and feared God﴾, meaning: opposing the Messenger, ﴿there is a great reward﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 173:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them"﴾. This is the statement of Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i. The story concerning this is: "When Abu Sufyan was unable to set out at the appointed time for Badr, he sent Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i to Medina and said to him: 'Discourage the companions of Muhammad from going out, so that they do not think we are weak, and you will have ten camels.' So he came to them, while the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions were preparing to go out. He said to them: 'Will you go out to them? They came out against you last year and did to you what they did in your homes. By God, if you go out to them, not one of you will return.' But he and his companions said: 'God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs,' and they did not refrain from going out."

As for His saying: ﴿Those to whom people said﴾, it refers to Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud alone. This is the statement of Ikrimah, Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Kalbi. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the statement of a small group from 'Abd al-Qays. As for His saying: ﴿So it increased them in faith﴾, some said its meaning is: it increased them in faith through their entrusting of their affairs (to God), and their saying: "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." It was also said its meaning is: it increased them in certainty regarding what God had promised them of victory. ﴿And they said, "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: this is the statement of Abraham when he was cast into the fire, for he said: "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 174:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they returned with a blessing from Allah and bounty﴾. The meaning of the verse: "The Prophet and his Companions went out for the appointment with Abu Sufyan at Badr, which was the gathering place of the markets of the Arabs. But they did not meet anyone there, since their coming out did not coincide with [Abu Sufyan's coming out]. So they engaged in trade there, and profited, and then departed." That is His saying: ﴿So they returned with a blessing from Allah and bounty﴾. So the blessing (ni'mah) is well-being (al-'afiyah), and the bounty (fadl) is the profit of the trade. ﴿No harm touched them, and they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 175:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens you of his allies﴾. "Shaytan" (Satan) is every rebellious, insolent one among the jinn and mankind. What is meant by "Shaytan" here is Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud. It is also said that it is the well-known Shaytan, for he whispered to them: "Do not go out for that promise."

As for His saying: ﴿frightens his allies﴾, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: its meaning is "frightens you of his allies," i.e., of his allies, who are the disbelievers. The people of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: this is a good view.

Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "frightens you with his allies," and thus Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited it. (Similar to it) is the Exalted's saying: ﴿to warn of a severe punishment﴾, i.e., with a severe punishment. The poet said:

(I commanded you to good, so do what I commanded you... for I have left you possessing wealth and lineage.)

i.e., I commanded you with good, so the preposition "bi" was dropped. ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.﴾

The Qur'an, 3:176 – Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And let them not grieve you﴾. It is also read "wa-la yuhzinka" with a damma on the yā' (yuḥzinuka), and both have the same meaning.

﴿Those who hasten into disbelief﴾: meaning, the speech of those who hasten into disbelief.

﴿Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all﴾: meaning, they will not diminish Allah in any way. ﴿Allah intends not to give them a share in the Hereafter﴾: meaning, a portion in the Hereafter. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾.

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who have bought disbelief in exchange for faith﴾. That is, they exchanged (استبدلوا), and every شِرَاء (purchase) is a استبدال (exchange), but not every استبدال is a شِرَاء. ﴿Will never harm Allah in the least﴾, that is, they will never diminish Allah in the least. ﴿And theirs is a painful punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 178:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose﴾, meaning: let them not think, from al-hisban (ḥisbān), which is supposition (al-ẓann), ﴿that Our giving them respite is good for their souls﴾. Al-imlā' (imlā', "respite") is prolonging the lifespan, and al-imhāl (imhāl, "delay") is postponement; and it is said that night and day are called mulawān (mulawān, "the two that alternate").

﴿Indeed, We give them respite only that they may increase in sin﴾, meaning: We only prolong their lifespans so that they may increase in sin. Al-Aswad narrated from Ibn Mas'ud: "There is no one but that death is better for him, whether he is righteous or wicked. As for the righteous, it is because of the saying of the Almighty: ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾. As for the wicked, it is because of the saying of the Almighty: ﴿Indeed, We give them respite only that they may increase in sin﴾; and that is because when he increases in sin, his punishment is intensified." ﴿And for them is a humiliating punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 179:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾, meaning: in the mixing of the hypocrites with you, for they were mixed in among the believers. ﴿Until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾. Mujahid said: "until He distinguishes the disbeliever from the believer." Qatadah said: "until He distinguishes the hypocrite from the believer." It is also read as "yumayyiz" with a doubled letter (shaddah), and it is said: māza yumayyizu and mayyaza yumayyizu, with the same meaning. And in a hadith: "Whoever removes (māza) harmful matter from the road, it is a charity for him." ﴿Nor would Allah disclose to you the unseen﴾. The occasion of its revelation: the Companions of the Messenger of Allah said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform us of who will die in faith and who will die in disbelief." So He revealed His saying: ﴿Nor would Allah disclose to you the unseen, but Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾. Meaning: He informs him of the unseen with what He wills. This is like His saying at the end of Surat al-Jinn: ﴿He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved﴾. ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Allah, you will have a great reward﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 180:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them﴾, meaning: it would be good for them. ﴿Rather, it is bad for them.﴾ There are two views regarding the meaning of the verse. The first is that it concerns the Jews, who concealed the description of Muhammad and withheld it. According to this view, His saying ﴿What they withheld will be tied around their necks on the Day of Resurrection﴾ means: the sin of what they withheld will be on them on the Day of Resurrection. The second view is that the verse concerns those who withhold zakat (obligatory almsgiving), and His saying ﴿What they withheld will be tied around their necks on the Day of Resurrection﴾ is to be taken literally. This is the meaning of what is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever withholds zakat, on the Day of Resurrection his wealth will be presented to him as a bald venomous snake (shuja' aqra'), and it will be coiled around his neck, and it will bite him from his forehead to his feet." Then he recited this verse. ﴿To Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth.﴾ If someone asks: How can the heavens and the earth be an inheritance for Him? It is said: The Arabs call everything that passes from one person to another an inheritance, by whatever cause it occurs. When the heavens and the earth became exclusively Allah's, after His servants had perished, He called it an inheritance, as though it had passed from them to Him. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 181:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich."﴾ It has been said: the occasion of the revelation of the verse was that when the verse ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ was revealed, the Jews said: "Indeed, Allah borrows from us our wealth; so then He is poor and we are rich." They did not say this out of conviction, but as a deception upon the Muslims and a means of creating doubt in them regarding what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, had brought. So the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich."﴾ There is another report concerning this: that when the Prophet (ﷺ) sought the help of the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa' in war, they said: "Then Allah is poor, since He seeks our help in supporting His religion; and we are rich." So the verse was revealed.

﴿We will record what they have said﴾: this is the recording in the scrolls of deeds. It has also been said that its meaning is: We will count what they said, and We will requite them for it. And it is read: "Sayaktubu mā qālū" (will be recorded what they said) with a dammah on the yā'. ﴿And their killing of the prophets﴾: in the nominative (marfū'), meaning: and their killing of the prophets will be recorded. ﴿Without right, and We will say: "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾ That is: with the punishment of the Fire, because the punishment of the Fire is burning.

﴿That is for what your hands have put forward﴾ — meaning: for what you have put forward; the mention of "your hands" is for emphasis.

﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ — meaning: that He does to them what He does as a recompense for their deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 183:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Those who say, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant that we not believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering which fire devours"﴾ — the verse is about the Jews. Al-Suddi said: Allah the Exalted had made a covenant with the Jews that they should not believe in a messenger until he brings them an offering which fire devours, except for Jesus and Muhammad. Allah commanded them to believe in both of them without this condition.

Others said: They would draw near to Allah by means of an offering, then take the choicest of its meat and place it in a house. Then their prophet would stand in that house communing with his Lord, and a white fire with a rushing sound would come down from heaven and consume it. This was a sign that the offering had been accepted.

﴿Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you speak of"﴾ — that is, with proofs and miracles, and "what you speak of" means the bringing of an offering which fire devours.

﴿Why then did you kill them﴾ — that is, why did you deny them and kill them, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your claim of that covenant.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 184:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied, who came with clear proofs﴾, that is, with evident signs and miracles, ﴿and the scriptures﴾: the plural of zabur (scripture), which is a book containing wisdom. It is from this that the Book of Dawud (David) was named "Zabur". In the codex of the people of Syria, the reading is "wa-bi-l-zubur" (and with the scriptures).

If one says: what is the difference between the zubur (scriptures) and the Book (al-kitab)? For He also said: ﴿and the scriptures and the illuminating Book﴾. It is said: al-kitab is a name for what is written, and it involves the joining of some words within it to others, which is the sense of "compilation" (al-damm). As for al-zubur, it is derived from al-zabr, which means reproach (al-zajr), so a zabur is a book containing admonitions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 185:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾. The "tasting" of death is a metaphor (majaz). The literal meaning of tasting (dhawq) is perceiving something (al-ihsas bi'l-shay'); since one perceives death, it is called "tasting" figuratively. The poet said:

(Whoever does not die in youthful vigour will die in old age... Death is a cup, and every person will taste it.)

If someone says: "It is not hidden that every soul dies, so what is the benefit in His saying: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾?" It is said: He intended by it to encourage asceticism regarding this world (al-tazhid bi'l-dunya), meaning that souls are heading toward annihilation, so be ascetic toward the world. ﴿And you will only be paid your rewards on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire﴾, i.e., is saved (najja), and is distanced from the Fire, ﴿and is admitted to Paradise has succeeded﴾, i.e., has been saved (najja). ﴿And the life of this world is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾, because it deceives a person, and it is cut off (al-inqita').

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 186:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You will surely be tested﴾ meaning: you will surely be tested (litukhtabarunna), and it was said: you will surely be afflicted (lataṣābunna). ﴿in your wealth and your selves﴾: in your wealth through spending (in the way of Allah), and in your selves through jihad. It was also said: in your wealth [and your selves through calamities and illnesses]. Some of the people of spiritual insight (ahl al-khawatir) said: in your wealth through withholding it from the truth, and in your selves through following desire (al-hawa).

﴿And you will surely hear much hurtful speech from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah.﴾ Al-Zuhri said: this was about Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, who used to satirize the Prophet and insult the Muslims with his satire. It was also said: it refers to the saying of the Jews, "Uzayr is the son of Allah," and the saying of the Christians, "The Messiah is the son of Allah," and it was also said: it refers to the words of those who said, "Allah is poor."

﴿And if you are patient﴾ meaning: in the face of the harm, ﴿and maintain taqwa﴾ meaning: from opposing the Messenger, ﴿then indeed that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾ meaning: of the true realities of affairs and their hardships.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 187:

The word of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book, [saying], "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it."﴾ It was also said: it refers to all scholars. Allah took a covenant from the scholars that they should make knowledge clear to the people and not conceal it. And in a hadith: "Whoever is asked about a knowledge and conceals it, will be bridled with a bridle of fire."

﴿But they cast it behind their backs﴾, meaning: they abandoned it, casting it behind their backs, and ﴿exchanged it for a small price﴾, meaning: bribery. ﴿And wretched is what they purchase.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 188:

God the Exalted said: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have been given﴾, meaning: the Jews, [who rejoice] in what they have been given, namely the knowledge and the Book, yet they did not act in accordance with its requirements and what it demands. It was also said: it refers to the hypocrites who rejoice in what they have done of staying behind from the Messenger of God.

﴿And love to be praised for what they have not done﴾ (meaning): by false excuses. ﴿Then do not think them safe from the punishment﴾, i.e., safe from the punishment, ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾.

It is related that Marwan sent to ʿĀʾishah: "Then we are ruined, for we rejoice in what we do, and we love to be praised for what we have not done; and God the Exalted says: ﴿Do not think them safe from the punishment﴾." So ʿĀʾishah mentioned that the verse concerns the Jews.

Almost. The passage: God's saying, "And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is over all things capable" (Q. 3:189). He mentioned this as a rebuttal of their saying, "Indeed God is poor and we are rich."

Almighty God says: (Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of the night and the day, there are signs for people of understanding). That is: in them there are indications of His oneness for those possessed of intellect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 191:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾. Ibn Mas'ud and Imran ibn Husayn narrated that the Prophet said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then lying on your side, signalling with gestures." This is the meaning of the verse.

It was also said: its meaning is: those who affirm the oneness of Allah in every state.

﴿And they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, deducing from it His oneness. In a hadith: "Reflect upon the creation, but do not reflect upon the Creator."

﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain﴾, meaning: without purpose. It was also said: (in vain) means: with falsehood.

﴿Glory be to You﴾: this is for declaring You free of every imperfection. ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "I spent the night at the house of my aunt Maymunah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his wife slept lengthwise on the pillow, and I slept across its length. Then he got up during the night and recited these ten verses." In another narration he said: "He said: Glory be to the King, the Holy, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit," and he recited these ten verses to the end of the surah.

"His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, indeed You whomever You admit to the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him.﴾ That is, You have destroyed him. If someone says: Do you not say that the believers abide forever in the Fire, yet they do not enter it? How then is that a destruction? It is said: Qatadah said: The meaning of the verse: Indeed, whoever You admit to the Fire for eternal abiding, You have certainly disgraced him, that is, You have destroyed him. And al-Dahhak said: The meaning of the verse ﴿Indeed, whoever You admit to the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him﴾ is: You have exposed him and torn away his veil. According to this, it applies to everyone who enters the Fire, even if he does not abide in it forever. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾"

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 193:**

﴿Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, "Believe in your Lord," so we have believed﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that the caller is the Messenger. It was said that the caller is the Qur'an, as stated by Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, because many people did not see the Messenger and did not hear him.

﴿Our Lord, so forgive us our sins﴾, that is, our major sins, ﴿and remove from us our misdeeds﴾, that is, our minor sins. It was said that "sins" (dhunub) means acts of disobedience, and "misdeeds" (sayyi'at) means shortcomings in acts of worship.

﴿And take us in death with the righteous﴾. The "righteous" (al-abrar) are the obedient. It is reported in the traditions: "Indeed, the righteous does not harm the ant (dharr)," meaning the small red ants.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 194:

﴿Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ That is: through the tongues of Your messengers. ﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾ That is: do not expose us, and do not destroy us.

﴿Indeed, You do not break the promise﴾ This is in the manner of praising Him, because we know with certainty that You do not break the promise.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 195:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So their Lord responded to them: "I will not allow the work of any worker among you to be lost, whether male or female."﴾ It is related that Umm Salamah said to the Messenger of Allah: "I see that Allah does not mention women in the Qur'an." So there was revealed His saying: ﴿"Whether male or female; some of you are from others."﴾ That is, you are all like a single soul, so I will not lose the work of any one of you.

﴿Then those who emigrated, were expelled from their homes, were harmed in My cause, fought, and were killed﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: "were killed and fought" (wa-qutilu wa-qatalu). ﴿I will surely remove from them their misdeeds and admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah.﴾ That is, a recompense from Allah. ﴿And Allah has with Him the best of rewards.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Let not the strutting about of those who disbelieve in the land deceive you﴾. That is: (do not be deceived by) their being given free rein to pursue their aims, for their final destination is the Fire.

﴿A brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting-place.﴾ In it is evidence that the least of Paradise is better than this world. In a hadith: "The place of a whip in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 198:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But those who fear their Lord—for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever—as a provision (nuzul) from Allah.﴾ The nuzul (provision for a guest) is what is prepared for the guest of blessings. So Allah, exalted is He, named what He prepared for the believers of the delights of Paradise a nuzul from Allah. ﴿And that which is with Allah is better for the righteous.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 199:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah﴾. It is said: he meant al-Najashi (the Negus). It is narrated that when he died, the Prophet said to his companions: "Pray over your brother who has died, Ashama al-Najashi." The hypocrites said: "Look, he prays over a foreigner (ʿilj) of the Christians and supplicates for him!" So the verse was revealed.

It is also said: it concerns ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and those who embraced Islam with him. This is His statement: ﴿Those among them who believe in Allah, and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbling themselves before Allah﴾, that is, humble before Allah, ﴿and do not sell the signs of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 3, verse 200:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, be patient﴾, meaning: in jihad, ﴿and endure﴾, that is: alongside the enemies, ﴿and be steadfast﴾, that is: at the frontiers (thughur) by staying on constant guard. It was also said: be patient in your religion, endure alongside the enemies, and be steadfast by guarding the prayers. And in a hadith: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not direct you to that by which Allah erases sins and raises ranks?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Performing ablution thoroughly in difficult conditions, walking many steps to the congregations, and waiting for one prayer after another prayer. That is ribat, that is ribat, that is ribat."

﴿And fear Allah that you may prosper﴾, that is: be hopeful of success (al-falah).
